utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today is Thursday, 20th of March, 2008. My greetings to the Prosecution, to Mr. Seselj, and to all the people helping us. As you know, today's hearing will be devoted to video viewings. I suppose that Mr. Seselj has received in his own language from the Prosecution a list of the videotapes that are planned today and are going to be shown by themes. Has this been done, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It has indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, have you received this list in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent. The Trial Chamber is now in the hands of the technicians. They're going to show us the video clips, but beforehand can the Prosecution tell us where the videotape comes from, who took the footage or made the video, and what type of video it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, let me say good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom on this, the first day of spring, 2008. The first video has already been admitted. It's P62. This clip which runs for approximately 35 seconds is from the BBC documentary "Death of Yugoslavia - Wars of Independence." The "Death of Yugoslavia" series was produced by the Brook Lapping production company. It first aired on the BBC in the autumn of 1995. That portion from the documentary which includes an interview with Dr. Seselj was conducted by Laura Silber in early March 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I have a question regarding this BBC documentary. We hear about it everywhere. I even know that at the ICJ in the case of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina versus the Republic of Serbia and Montenegro this documentary has also been used. We also know that on several occasions Mr. Seselj challenged this. There's one thing I don't know because I've never seen the whole documentary as such, how long -- how many minutes is it, or how many hours is it, this documentary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My understanding, Mr. President, is the entire documentary runs approximately six hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Six hours you say. I see. Very well. Let us start with this snippet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Vojislav Seselj: The very roots of the Serbian cause are under threat. Hordes of Ustashas are attacking Serbian villages, Serbian women and children. The Ustasha hordes are trying to finalise the genocide of the Serbian nation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again for the record, that was P62. The next video on the list again has already been admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One minute, please. So this has already been admitted, hasn't it. At this juncture, Mr. Seselj, do you have any observations? I'm not asking you to testify, I'm just asking you whether you have a short comment so that it be acted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not testifying about anything, Mr. President. I'd just like to remind you of my two written submissions in which my associates explained the way in which videotapes are manipulated. I think this is too brief an excerpt for anyone to understand anything. I don't have anything against this. It is what I said it is, my sentence, and I would repeat it anywhere and everywhere. I'm not questioning its authenticity but this is just one sentence. I would like to see a broader excerpt so that you can see the context and why this speech was delivered in the first place. I can't see that from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can move on to the next clip, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The booth would like to know whether you wish the transcript to be read out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Show us the second clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps the Chamber could give some guidance. I heard the interpreter ask if the Chamber would like the interpreters to read out the transcript or if we simply want to have the rolling transcript played with the tapes. Well, certainly the transcript is certainly embedded in the videos but the question apparently from the booth is whether the Chamber would like the interpreters to also speak or read what's contained on the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When we see the footage and when there is a comment by the journalist because more often than not it is either the journalist commenting footage or Mr. Seselj speaking, then the interpreters have to translate into English and into French what Mr. Seselj says in his language, or if this is the journalist, an English speaker who makes a commentary, the interpreters have to translate into Mr. Seselj's language and into French what the journalist is saying. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next video is again already in evidence. This is P59. This runs approximately 1 minute and 40 seconds. This is material, archival material, obtained by the Office of the Prosecution from Croatian TV, HRT. It was provided to the Tribunal or to the Office of the Prosecutor on 20 March 1996 by the War Crimes Commission Zagreb pursuant to a request for assistance of 19 February 1996. Again, this is P59.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Journalist: I am jumping ahead a bit. Are your volunteers fall within 'paramilitary formations.' "Vojislav Seselj: We're not forming any kind of paramilitary formations here in this narrowed down Serbia. We're only gathering volunteers here and sending them where they're needed, to Serbia and Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem and Serbian Krajina. And these volunteers, they're placed under the command of local commanders, the Serbs who live there and carry out orders regarding their activities on the battlefield. Therefore, we are not engaged in establishing any paramilitary formations here and we oppose any kind of paramilitary formations. "Journalist: And are you the commander of all those forces? "Vojislav Seselj: Yes, of those volunteer forces which are there. "Journalist: And have you control over the situation? "Vojislav Seselj: Yes, I have control. So far I've always exercised control over the situation and all our volunteers are very well disciplined. We do not have any problems with them. We prohibit the use of any alcohol and take only those who are capable to fight, who are disciplined, who execute all tasks without objection, who above all act valiantly towards the enemy, and you will not be able to find any Croat who will complain about maltreatment unless he had a weapon in his hands and was attacking Serbian villages. In particular, you will not be able to find a single Croatian woman or child who would complain about mistreatment by Serbs which is not the case with the Croats who are once again making themselves noticeable by perpetrating awful crimes against the population."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis. Did you want to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give the floor to Mr. Seselj, but I noticed one thing in this clip. Is the translation correct? Because in Serbian it might not be the same word. However, this may have serious consequences. The journalist at some point says, "Are you the commander of all these forces?" And Mr. Seselj answered: "Yes. I am the commander of the volunteer forces which are there." In English this is what is being said. In the French translation that was the same, but I don't know what the journalist said in Serbian. Did the journalist say, "Are you the commander", or, "The man in charge"? Yes, Mr. Seselj, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm satisfied because it's direct exculpatory material. As far as I'm concerned, I really did say that I was the commander and that I have control. And you heard that it was said that they were under the command of the local commanders of the Territorial Defence in the operative sense, but I do have general control in the sense that I control discipline, conduct, and everything else. But there's something else that is essential here. When is the take dated? The Prosecutor said it was the second half of 1991, so that's my observation, because I find it favourable. Look at me on the tape. You can see white skin under the blue shirt and my face is suntanned because it was the summer, July. I was in the shade somewhere and you can see that I have this tan from the very hot sun. So it couldn't have been the second half of 1991. So the tape speaks for itself and says when this was taped. And this is obviously a time when we're sending direct volunteers to the Serbian villages under attack, under threat, and after the agreement of the JNA of the 1st -- with the JNA of the 1st of September, the JNA decided where our volunteers would be sent. So this is a vital point and two different things. So this cannot be incriminating material at all because it is not incorporated in the indictment. It is the period when the volunteers went illegally, as far as the Serb authorities were concerned, not through the JNA when they crossed the Danube illegally. So the most important point here is to note when this tape was taped, the date, and it can't be the second half of 1991. It was the first part of 1991 and July at the latest. It could be May or June, July as the latest month. Have a look again, you can see my white skin underneath my shirt and suddenly my face is all red and suntanned under the hot sun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have time to get a tan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber noticed that there is disagreement as to the date when this footage was taken. In the documents the Prosecution mentioned the second half of 1991, so that could be from July to December. It also appears that Mr. Seselj is wearing a summer shirt. He doesn't wear a jumper or a coat. So it could be June, he says, May. It could also be July or August. However, the Prosecution, when -- they could ask the Croatian television to know the exact date. That shouldn't be too difficult to do. Yes, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And another observation. Judging by the way in which the journalist spoke, this isn't Croatian television footage. It's something that came into the possession later on of Croatian television, because I think the journalist is speaking Ekavian, if I was able to follow. So it's not Croatian television as the source or perhaps a Serb journalist who did the work for them. That's not impossible either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In the French booth the interpreters would like to correct something. Which is the correction? The interpreter in the French booth has just confirmed what Mr. Seselj said, namely that volunteers are placed under the command of local commanders, and they carried out orders by the local commanders. This is what has just been said by the French interpreter. There was a part that was missing before when we viewed the clip. Very well. Let us move on to the third clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, before we do that, I simply for the benefit of the Trial Chamber would draw the Chamber's attention to the testimony of Dr. Seselj in the Milosevic case concerning the last video where he made very similar observations and comments to those he has just made concerning P59, and the Milosevic transcripts of 15 September 2005, at page 44137, contain the comments of Dr. Seselj concerning the last tape, and again they are more or less consistent with what he has just informed us, and I felt that the Chamber might want to review that with respect to this tape. The next video to be shown is actually two clips. There will be a brief pause between the two of them. This is again in evidence as P30. This is some of the raw footage from the interview of Dr. Seselj for "The Death of Yugoslavia" series. Again, this interview was taped in early March 1995. The Office of the Prosecutor received this material on 24 August 2005 from the producer of that series, again Brook Lapping productions. This interview was conducted by the journalist Laura Silber and was part of the footage taken for "The Death of Yugoslavia" series which aired in the BBC in the autumn of 1995. As I've indicated, there are two clips. The first one runs approximately 1 minute 15 seconds; the second one runs approximately 30 seconds and this is P30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] VS: In 1990, we were not acquiring weapons, we were only enlisting volunteers and occasionally sending them to the front lines if necessary from time to time. In 1991, we began organising volunteers on a larger scale and send them to the already formed fronts, especially Eastern Slavonia. Here in the east of the Republic of Serbian Krajina volunteers proved themselves especially in the battle in Borovo Selo which took place on May the 2nd, 1991, when they defeated the stronger Croatian forces, Croatian police and para-police forces. We were getting weapons from Milosevic's police from the then -- first from the then Minister of Internal Affairs Radmilo Bogdanovic and when he was replaced from his successor. We were also getting old weapons from the warehouse of the Territorial Defence. There were old American Thompson guns which had been withdrawn from use a long time ago. There were also M-48 guns out of date, the so-called Tandzare, what the enemy had stopped using a long time ago, what was kept somewhere in the warehouses of the Territorial Defence. They felt sorry to destroy it all so they just gave them to us, but it was with those weapons that we beat the Croats who were armed with modern weapons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, for a number of reasons this tape should be introduced if Laura Silber comes in as a Prosecution witness. This is the '95 tape when there was a great conflict with Milosevic, and you see the basic contradiction. I attacked Milosevic, Radmilo Bogdanovic who was the vice-president of the lower Chamber of the Federal Assembly and later I set out the fact that the arms come from the Territorial Defence and the JNA and not the police. So quite obviously there's some settling of accounts over there in Serbia between us where I use heavy artillery to attack Milosevic and there he is moving towards the Western forces waging a peaceful policy. So I think that I explained this, too, in the Slobodan Milosevic trial and the Prosecutor can remind us of that because he reads the transcripts. I don't read them; I don't need to. So the question of relevance here is twofold. Secondly, this obviously is an excerpt again because the Prosecution has in one of my books that I disclosed in 2003 in a set of 88 [as interpreted] books, the entire interview with Laura Silber. So it's better that they show you that on paper. As far as I know, they've also had it translated into English. Laura Silber worked with me, conducted an interview with me which lasted a total of one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seem to remember that indeed what Mr. Seselj has just said was said in the Milosevic trial. I believe that he said that this was against Mr. Milosevic. So he said that already. He's repeating it today, but you can find this in the Milosevic transcript. Okay. Let's move on to the second clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the second clip from P30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] VS: In May 1992, I began having meetings with Milosevic on a regular basis and back then it was always Milosevic himself who asked for volunteers to be sent out. I mean, one did not have convince us very much. We took this as our duty, our responsibility except when it came to the deployment where they were most needed because they were known as the bravest and the most capable and the most disciplined men."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the same explanation as the previous instance. What is correct here? My meeting with Milosevic is correct that took place in 1992, and having discussed what the Serbs in Bosnia would do when the JNA withdraws, and then on that occasion he said, "Well, you can continue to send volunteers." However, after May 1992, the Prosecution does not have a single shred of evidence about the involvement of the Serb authorities in sending out volunteers because the volunteers which we sent went in civilian clothing and they went almost incognito across the Drina River. So if the Prosecution does have some evidence to show that official Serbia helped this after May 1992, then this could be confirmation along with that, because this doesn't show anything in itself, especially since I deny it. This is just my attack on Milosevic to make it more difficult for him to draw closer to the Western powers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was already mentioned in Mr. Seselj's testimony in the Milosevic case, which has been tendered into evidence. Let's move on to the next clip, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next videotape clip is 65 ter number 6029, the old 65 ter number was 2066. This was a videotape received from Natasha Kandic on April 1, 1996. That's the date the Prosecution received this tape. It's a compilation of Serbian television broadcasts, mainly news broadcasts. The date of this material was either 2 or 3 November 1991, according to our records. This is 65 ter number 6029. This clip runs approximately 48 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Announcer 3: Volunteers from Kosovo and Metohija today headed for the battlefield. We have a report from Pristina about that from our colleague Milivoje Mihajlovic. "MM: This is how the first of the volunteers from Kosovo and Metohija going on an organised basis to the battlefield in Croatia were seen off last night not long after midnight. Around 50 Vukovar -- about 50 volunteers from this southern province went to -- this volunteers unit was formed in Pristina as early as the beginning of summer and its commanding officer, Dragisa Vukcevic, is the manager of the local hotel company Sloga. Volunteers are well equipped and in the past months their commanding officers have been emphasising their non-affiliation to any party."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to Mr. Seselj, let me say this: We've just discovered this video clip for the first time. I just make a personal observation. There are many volunteers. All of them are -- look tidy, are shaven, and they are in military uniforms with a cap and an insignia on them. So they seem to have been gathered before boarding buses in a hotel. That's what the video clip said. They get on the buses in order to go somewhere else, to another location. This is my personal observation of the video clip. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm a little worried by that comment of yours, Mr. President. I would like the Prosecution to find at least one volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party who is dirty and unkept, unwashed. With a beard, yes, but not unkept and dirty. Let them find just one if they can. Now, you saw at the end of this tape that the speaker says that it is volunteers outside the party, which -- any party, which means no party is involved. It's the volunteers that have rallied together from Pristina. A unit was established and they were sent to the Sid army barracks for training and they were sent to the front after that. Now, the relevance of all this here is the question that arises. What has that got to do with these proceedings? There were various volunteers throughout the war. They weren't all volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party and here is proof of that. This is proof that they were not and this is exculpatory material, as far as I'm concerned. Once again I'm not against it. I want it to be part of the record to show that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So you don't have any objection. We can give a number to this clip immediately. Can we have a number, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The video clip shall be given Exhibit number P00286. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next videotape bears 65 ter 4143. That's 4143. The old 65 ter number was 0298. This is a clip that runs approximately 16 seconds. It's from a documentary produced by the B-92 broadcasting company called "Vukovar, The Final Cut." This documentary was produced in 2006. The Office of the Prosecution received this videotape from the B-92 broadcast service on March 3, 2006.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover]Goran Milicevic: The order comes. Let the old people go. The Chetniks are coming. Listen, we looked after you as much as we could. The Chetniks are coming. We do not guarantee."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I remind you of the previous clip. You saw the uniforms and the berets on the heads of the volunteers from Pristina. Did you notice that all of them have berets? They don't have five-star -- five-pointed star and obviously they had been given uniforms by the JNA. What does it mean here when the speaker says the Chetniks are coming? What Chetnik? Were all the Chetniks in the war the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party? If this is the Prosecutor's thesis then they should confirm that. Nothing can be discerned from this clip here. Yesterday you saw Witness Cakalic who spoke about the local Chetniks from Vukovar of whom he recognised some and gave us their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, it's a video clip that lasts only 16 seconds, so obviously everything goes very fast. I've got two questions. When was this video footage taken, and where, because we see that fire is being opened. There are civilians there. Everything moves very quickly, but I have no idea where it is and when it is. Do you have any idea about this? Do you have any idea about the date and of the place where these -- this footage was taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, all the information that we have is that it came from the television company B-92 in Belgrade. We received it on March 3, 2006. It was from a documentary produced by B-92 entitled "Vukovar, The Final Cut." That's all the information we have concerning this video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must draw your attention to the fact that B-92 is an American spy organisation which was directly funded from the source fund and from the funds of the Western intelligence services throughout all this time, from its beginning to this very day, and I have mentioned it on a number of my interviews and the Prosecution can find it in a number of my interviews. I publicly accused this TV company of being an American spy, Natasha Kandic and B-92 alike. If you now admit into the file the interpretation of their journalists about something, then you have to know that this is always going to be an interpretation against the Serbian people, against the Serbian Radical Party and against me personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, do you challenge the admission of this video clip? Because you're telling us that B-92 is in the pay of the Americans who, if I understand correctly, are against the Serbs. But you did not tell us what your position is. Are you in favour or against the admission this video clip, because this could be a clip in your favour or not in your favour. So what is your position exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this clip cannot either harm me or benefit me. It doesn't say a thing. So why would I object its admission? It doesn't say a thing. I'm not objecting. You do whatever. Why would I object to this footage? It does not threaten me in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are going to ask the registrar to give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be Exhibit number P00287. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6040. It's 6040. The old 65 ter number was 2241. This is video footage dated 20 November 1991. It was film that was used in the -- or for the defence of Slavko Dokmanovic. Based on our information, this was amateur footage coming from the defence of Slavko Dokmanovic and shows members of the Serbian Autonomous District of the SBSW, including Mr. Dokmanovic, Goran Hadzic, and Zeljko Raznjatovic also known as Arkan. This is 65 ter number 6040.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again we have a video clip where things are moving extremely quickly. The only observation a reasonable trier of fact can make when watching this video is that we have two things here. We have a great number of soldiers wearing military uniforms or camouflage uniforms. Second thing, we see armoured vehicles next to these soldiers, and we can see a soldier who apparently has been wounded to the hand and is holding a dog. And at the end of the video we see a number of buses stationed there. A few words, that's the description of this video footage. We see a number of individuals. I don't know them. It may be Goran Hadzic, Kameni, Arkan, but I don't know these people. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the soldier with the dog whose arm had been wounded is Arkan, and the blonde soldier towards the end of the footage is Milan Lancuzanin, Kameni. Where is manipulation here? Zeljko Raznjatovic, also known as Arkan, and Milan Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni, in Vukovar. This is what it says on the paper and my conclusion is that they were taken together but they're nowhere -- nowhere together. I don't know whether they ever met in their whole life. I only met Arkan on a couple of occasions in my whole life, but I'm not sure that Kameni ever met him. I'm raising the question of relevance here. Why is the Prosecutor's office trying to have this admitted. I'm not objecting. If you are not threatening the overload of your file, then why should I object? I'm not objecting, but I'm raising the issue of relevance here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have only one question, Mr. Seselj. Was this video footage taken in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judging by everything, it was in Vukovar, but how come Kameni is in the footage? Kameni must have been shot here in Vukovar. Arkan could have been shot somewhere else, because Arkan's units was to the north of Vukovar and Leva Supoderica that Kameni was in command of was in the Sector South. These two units throughout the war did not have any contact. Kameni was under the command of the commander of the 1st Guards Brigade and Arkan was under the command of the commander of the Novi Sad Corps. You could see this from the documents that have already been presented and admitted through some witnesses. I'm not doubting that this was Vukovar. I'm sure -- I suppose that this was Vukovar. I'm just raising the issue of relevance and I'm not objecting to the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that this footage was taken in Vukovar. The only thing you're challenging is that you challenge that Kameni and Arkan would have been there together on the 20th of November at 3.42 p.m., because I believe that this footage was shot at 3.42 p.m. It's been recorded on the transcript now. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot swear that they never met, but this is not what can be deducted from this video, and this is the essence. I -- on the anniversary of the liberation of Vukovar I was there. There were many people there, Major Sljvancanin, Radic. I met Arkan in Beli Manastir on the anniversary of the liberation of Baranja, you know. These meetings are not impossible but this video clip is not the one to prove that there indeed was a meeting between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Registrar could we have a number please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That would be Exhibit number P00288. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next videotape bears 65 ter number 6038, 6038. Old 65 ter number 2240. This videotape which runs 2 minutes 50 seconds is from the British network ITN. The tape was labelled "Vukovar, 19 November 1991." The Prosecution received this videotape from the British network ITN on 4 March 1996, and this contains a report by ITN reporter Michael Nicholson. This is 65 ter number 6038.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Unidentified soldier: There is, there is, it will be done. "Unidentified man: I'm not the one who needs it, my brother. Let me only be safe and sound and my child. And I spent three months in a cellar. I did not see the outside world. From Belgrade to be here an ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to start again. We have no sound.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Unidentified soldier: There is, there is, it will be done. "Unidentified man: I'm not the one who needs it, my brother. Let me only be safe and sound and my child. And I spent three months in a cellar. I did not see the outside world. From Belgrade to be here is an ... "Pedja: What television are you from? "Journalist: ITN London. "Pedja: Will they lie about us again? "Journalist: No. "Pedja: Why did they lie about Dubrovnik? That one [unintelligible] shaved down there."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Unidentified soldier: There is, there is, let you be. It will be done. "Unidentified man: I'm not the one who needs it, my brother. Let me only be safe and sound and my child. And I spent three months in a cellar. I didn't see the outside world. From Belgrade to be here as an ... "Pedja: What television are you from? "Journalist: ITN London. "Pedja: Will they lie about us again? "Journalist: No. "Pedja: Why did they lie about Dubrovnik? That one [unintelligible] shaved down there ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We run into some technical problems, but eventually we managed to play this video. A reasonable trier of fact may conclude that in this video we have two parts. In the first part of the video we see a column of the people who are walking down the main street, apparently. There is music playing in the background. We see a soldier kissing a child. The people we see there, the civilians, men, women, and children, do not seem to be frightened at all. The first question, therefore, is to know whether these people are civilian or Serb -- Croatian or Serb civilians. And in the second part of this video, the clip that was meant to be shown to us, apparently, we see people climbing out of their cellars. Apparently they spent several days, even several weeks in the cellars, and we could believe and conclude that this happens just shortly after the fighting. My fellow Judge wants to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wanted to ask whether the house we see in the first part of the footage is the headquarters of the volunteers. I'm talking about the house with the black flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not in a position to comment on that, and I believe that perhaps the best thing to do would be to ask some of the subsequent witnesses who might be in a position to identify that. I would be hesitant to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It's -- it's -- sorry. I'm asking because it is indicated in the list that there is a footage of the Chetniks' headquarters, and I'm just wondering what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With a question mark, I believe, as well indicating that there's some uncertainty as to that point. I would expect that we will have witnesses that this tape could be shown to who would be in a position to identify that house or that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Seselj, your comments?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, obviously this could not have been the 19th of November. This could only be the 18th of November. If you noticed, you could still hear shooting at the beginning of the footage. On the day when the civilians came out of the shelters is the day when Vukovar was liberated, on the 18th. There is no criteria according to which you may distinguish the Serb civilians from the Croat civilians. I suppose that the majority must have been Croats but they came out of the shelters together. And one more thing, there's no criteria according to which the Prosecutor can make a distinction between a JNA soldier and a volunteer. It may be done with the Territorial Defence, because with the Territorial Defence the uniforms were incomplete. The parts were civilian, parts were military because they did not have uniform storages from which they could dress themselves. Volunteers, on the other hand, were all wearing complete uniforms. They had come in them in -- from Serbia, and they are -- they put the uniforms on in the barracks in Bubanj Potok. And as for the Chetnik headquarters, this is pure manipulation. The Prosecutor is duty-bound to tell you here based on which could he write in the paper that this was a footage of Chetniks headquarters. What is the indicia? What is the proof? Where does this come from? He first put it on paper and then they're going to look for witnesses that may be able to confirm this. There was no headquarters of Chetniks there. There was no Chetnik headquarters in Vukovar up to the moment that Vukovar was liberated and there was no Chetnik organisation together with the existing JNA. There is an identification with a majority of volunteers in the Territorial Defence with the Chetnik Movement, because this is a good and nice Serbian tradition that the Communists tried to eradicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your comments are on the record. There's something I wanted to say earlier on. I'm going to say it now. Do we know whether these people are Serb or Croatian civilians? In the second part of the video, not in the first part. In the second part we see an individual leaving a house, and he says that he's been there for quite some time, and then he adds the words "from Belgrade." "From Belgrade." We might infer from that that this individual before being there was in Belgrade. If you like, we can show this again. We heard him say "from Belgrade." Is it a Croat who used to live in Belgrade and who came there or is it a Serb? But this person spontaneously said "of Belgrade." The comments of Mr. Seselj have been recorded on the transcript are, and there's the issue here of the headquarters of the volunteers possibly. The only thing we can say is that we see a building with a flag. That's the only information we can draw from the video. Let's proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would ask that that tape be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That will be Exhibit number P00289. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip to be shown has already been admitted into evidence. This is P20. This is a documentary film produced by the foundation The Right To Pictures And Words. This film or this clip from the documentary entitled "Vukovar 1991, Images And Words Of Hate." This clip runs approximately 35 seconds and again has already been admitted into evidence as P20.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: Here we are standing on the Vuka River bridge. The Vuka River gave the name to this town Vukovar. The Croats call it Stalingrad. "Pedja: No way, man, no. Stalingrad, only in their stories can they call it Stalingrad. Where the army and the Serbian volunteers tread nothing can help them. They can call it what they want. Freedom has come and this freedom will the not be sold easy to anyone anymore. "Reporter: Are you a volunteer or are you from around here. "Pedja: I'm volunteer from Sombor, but I intend settle down here and live in this pretty town. Even demolished like this it's still pretty. Even demolished it's still pretty to me, by the way. I'm Pedja from Sombor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, just the question of relevance. It's obviously a volunteer from Sombor. That's what it's about. After Vukovar fell or prior to the fall and the liberation and he expresses the desire to stay on and live in Vukovar. There were a number of people like that. I know several. Maybe there were more than several who stayed on and lived in Vukovar after the war. Some got married there. They met young women there and married them. But once again the question of relevance. Now, I didn't hear the Prosecutor properly. This footage was done by a foundation the right to freedom and speech, something like that. I've never heard of a foundation with that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where does this tape come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, again, we received this from B-92 on the 8th of May, 2001, and according to the information provided to us, it was a documentary film produced by the foundation, which is called The Right To Pictures And Words. So B-92 provided this to us. It's a documentary produced by the Right To Pictures And Words Foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see the picture of the volunteer again, because on his cap he has an insignia which is very visible. Could we see this picture again, the picture of the volunteer. My colleague tells me that he has, too, so all the more reason to see this again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: Here we are standing on the Vuka River bridge, the Vuka River gave the name to its town Vukovar. The Croats call it Stalingrad. "Pedja: What do you mean Stalingrad? Only in their stories can they call it Stalingrad. Where the army and the Serbian volunteers tread nothing can help them. They can call it what they want."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague tells me that one can see two insignia. The first one which is in direct line with his nose but you also see something which is cross-shaped. He wears a cap with an insignia on it. If there are no further observations, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand where you see the other badge on the level of the nose. The insignia on the beret is the same as it is on the berets of the volunteers from Pristina. Now what does it contain. It's a cockade with the old traditional Serbian coat of arms, the laurel leaf symbol. So there's no skull and bone insignia or anything else and it's the same as the cockade of the volunteers you saw from Pristina. It's exactly the same. You can compare the footage. Now, this other sign there, I didn't see that. I don't know what you're referring to. You said at the level of the nose? What?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see that alongside it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Stop there. As you can see, next to the insignia, on the left-hand side of the insignia you see something which is cross shaped.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's -- that seems to me to be a beret, a foreign -- a foreign manufacture. There was something on the beret, and the trace remained. It's not something that's on the beret now. It was something that was on the beret before the cockade with the Serb insignia was placed. You can see the imprint of a cross. Perhaps it's a sports organisation or something. It's difficult to say what. But what the soldier wanted to place on his beret was the traditional Serbian cockade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This video had already been admitted under the number P20. Let's move on to the next pictures, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6036. The old number was 0732. This is a clip which runs approximately 30 seconds. This tape was received by Natasha Kandic on the 1st of April, 1996. Again, it is a compilation of Serb -- Serbian television news broadcasts. The date that accompanied this material when it was logged into the OTP system was 16, 17 November 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I have a question for you. You told us on several occasions that Natasha Kandic had sent you the videos. Does this mean that the OTP receives any document, any video sent by anyone or do you select the material you receive and only keep what you feel is important, and you set aside some of the things that are being sent to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, obviously the Office of the Prosecutor receives information, material, documents, videos, et cetera, from a wide range of sources. Quite often witnesses have videotapes. They hand them over. If the videotape or any other material that anyone submits purports to be authentic and relevant to any ongoing investigation, of course the investigators will -- will take that material and enter it into the evidence pipeline. It would be hard to imagine an investigator who when someone offers him or her relevant material would turn that away. So clearly we do receive material from a wide range of sources. That does not necessarily mean that everything that we receive would eventually be tendered into a court proceeding, but certainly unless there's some reason to doubt that the material relates to the conflict in the former Yugoslavia, we would certainly take that material and enter it into the evidence pipeline. With respect to Ms. Kandic, of course, we receive material from a large number of NGOs, both small NGOs as well as larger ones that the general public is aware of. So there's a wide range of NGOs across entire spectrums of various interests that have provided the Office of the Prosecutor with evidentiary material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question of a technical nature to put to you, Mr. Mundis. The OTP receives information, as you've just told us, of any kind, amongst others videos which you are able to identify, and you identify these as coming from various media sources abroad. But what I would like to know, at the OTP do you have any technicians, people of course who are of a great quality and who are capable based on material like videos to determine whether the video has been tampered with, has been edited? Did you have experts or technical engineers, highly qualified technical engineers who would be capable on the basis of the videos to detect any form of tampering or that somebody had input items from outside or data from outside and integrate it into the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The short answer to that question is no. When material -- when we have reason to believe that material might have been tampered with or it becomes challenged in court cases, the material is sent to outside forensic laboratories for analysis. As Your Honours will probably appreciate and can understand, quite often when we receive tapes we are not receiving the original tape. That is, we are receiving something that perhaps someone had videotaped at home off of a television newscast or it's a copy of a copy of a tape that someone produces or provides to us and as a result of that in many, but not all, but in many instances it is not possible forensically to determine if the original tape had in any way been altered because what the expert's dealing with is a copy of a copy and not the original tape itself. So quite often there are -- there are indicia that it's simply inconclusive. A forensic expert will review this material and it will be inconclusive as to whether there was any tampering simply because forensic experts will, as a general rule, require the original tape in order to make that kind of determination as to whether there was any tampering at the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Judges, that it was -- it is with good reason that the Prosecution has full trust -- places full trust in Natasha Kandic, because she is the main instructor of the false witnesses for The Hague in Belgrade. So they have every reason to believe her. Of all the Serb spies in the American service, Natasha Kandic occupies the number one position. So it's quite clear to me why the Prosecution refers to her. She was in the public gallery a few days ago and I almost burst out laughing out loud. She controlled witness Stoparic, and then we have a tape of her message. So one should bear all that mind. So I quite understand why the Prosecution places great trust in Natasha Kandic. They have to do so. As far as they're concerned, she's a great authority for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you are responsible for your own words. You are saying that Mrs. Natasha Kandic instrumentalised false witnesses. You are saying that she works for services.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you began speaking just now I've heard nothing through the headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat. I was saying, Mr. Seselj, that what you have said about Mrs. Natasha Kandic is on your own responsibility. You said that she instrumentalised false witnesses. You are saying that she works for the American intelligence services. You are the one to say that. It's for you to demonstrate the truthfulness of what you are saying but the issue doesn't hinge on that as far as we're concerned. What we are interested in is to know whether there's any form of technical control on the videos. The Prosecutor has told us that this is just about impossible because they do not have the original copies and on the original videos and it's very difficult to do this kind of work on a video which is not an original video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I would also like to emphasise this: Mr. Seselj should avoid making any comments about any individuals, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor. Can you show us the next video, please, 6036.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at this point, the Prosecution will simply reserve any possible responses to attacks by Dr. Seselj on Ms. Kandic, but we may in the future need to return to that issue. The next videotape as I've indicated bears 65 ter number 6036.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Novinar: Here on the front lines on Trpinja road we also met soldiers ... "Zivkovic: Zivkovic Vojislav, a Seselj volunteer. "Draganic: Draganic Ranko, a volunteer from Indija. "Novinar: When did you arrive and since when have you been fighting here at the front lines. "Zivkovic: Well, I myself came on the 15th of June and since then I've been at the front lines wherever needed in Dalj, in Salvas, and in Tenja, and here. "Reporter: Do they have a chance, the Ustashas? "Draganic: None. A bit longer and they're ours. "Reporter: You came here and you said you've been fighting since June. Tell us, are you under the command of the army or are you here as volunteers, in which manner are you here on the fighting lines. "Zivkovic: We're volunteers in cooperation with the army. We get all the orders from the army. We're not fighting on our own because the army is the one whom we are fighting with, their command. "Reporter: So that means you're not representing the goals of the party here but the orders and goals of the Yugoslav People's Army and the entire Serbian people. "Zivkovic: Exactly. We are reluctant to speak about being Seselj's men because now is not the time to talk about that. There will be time for that when this is over. Then when we can talk, but right now we're fighting for Serbian land."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This video which is an interview of a -- of a volunteer, the volunteer answers a question put by the journalist purportedly of Novi Sad. He says that he's a volunteer and that they're acting jointly with the army. He is saying, "We are getting our orders from the army." It's their command. This is what this volunteer says. Let me add that we can see this volunteer. He is wearing an armband on his left arm and something which looks like an insignia on his chest, which we could see again perhaps. So, Mr. Seselj, your comments.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am very pleased that you had an opportunity to see real Seselj volunteers and so that you can establish that they're -- that they look decent, that they have their uniforms on, and that you don't ascribe to Seselj volunteers everybody who is dirty, unkept, drunk, under the influence of drugs or who knows what else. This is an example of what the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party looked like. The bands around their arms are ones which certain units had in order to be able to distinguish each other in an action. And you can ask military experts. Sometimes you put a band on an epaulette and other times around the arm. That's so that they can distinguish themselves and avoid sort of friendly fire because sometimes the other side wearing Yugoslav Army uniforms too. But what I would like to say here is something else. They are two volunteers in Vukovar and there was a description of where they went into action, Dalj, Salvas, and so on. Tenja is a suburb of Osijek. So bear that in mind or perhaps this was at the Trpinjska road. That's not impossible, too. So that was to the north towards Vukovar but mostly they held the line towards Osijek, if you have an idea of the configuration. Osijek is at the confluence of the Drava and Danube rivers but it's another municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I have understood you correctly you do not object to the tendering into evidence of this video. Let's have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am grateful to the Prosecution for offering up this video footage and for tendering it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next -- the video clip that was just shown shall be given Exhibit number P00290. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break we shall see another video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next videotape or clip is a second clip, actually, from the same 65 ter number, that is 65 ter number 6036. The source is the same as indicated for the last clip. This clip runs about two and a half minutes and contains information from the Novi Sad television daily news from 16/17 November 1991 and contains an interview with Major Sljvancanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] J: Today the units of the Yugoslav People's Army have taken control of the Vukovar city centre. Apart from that, the fighting has been continued against the forces, the most hardened Ustasha forces still holding some check-points or strongholds. Major, I would like to ask you briefly to describe for us today's combat activities here in this area. "VS: Well, all the units in the territory of Vukovar fight under the unified command of the south operation groups and under the command of the Yugoslav People's Army which is very important because volunteers often say you never mention us and then I think we're all the same kind and we fight under the same command for the same goals and they all reported to us. We accept everyone who ever comes, every volunteer and every well-meaning person. We equip them right away, prepare them for combat, include them in the units of the JNA. They carry out combat activities side by side with other soldiers. The enemy, that is the Ustashas, are completely defeated. We control the whole situation in Vukovar. There are only a couple more streets left where the most hardened Ustashas are hiding and who at this moment offered to surrender to us and ask about the conditions of their surrender. We gave them a promise but sometimes someone gets to the station possibly even one of them one who bothers them who say they are Chetniks there, they would be slaughtered and else which disturbs them. Afterwards their leaders who have been in contact with them under the name of Jastreb and under other names no longer call them, they were absolutely quiet today. It is only a question of an hour or a day when a few of them who remain, the most hardened Ustashas will come out and surrender. Some groups have already surrendered last night and today we have saved a large number of civilians. Our soldiers and volunteers, call them as you like, have also done some heroic deeds, especially the ones from Vukovar who know the city go into basements at night and save people who are still in those basements and who are still frightened and who fear the Guards' members and Ustashas would come and slaughter them. And then when they explain the whole situation to them, they gladly accept crossing over the Yugoslav People's Army side and join our lines, our ranks and be given all the help they need. As you have seen, we are successful in doing this. We are saving a lot of innocent people who have been imprisoned in the basement so I think we're going to clear the remaining small number of streets during the day. We would like, and it is our goal, to make Vukovar a free city for all citizens and all people of goodwill. We wish to save our soldiers and our combatants and we don't want to push it now at the very end in order to achieve all our objectives. It is important to say the people can conquer all that and achieve the goal we set ourselves and we're probably going to make it; not probably but for sure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that it was too fast for them to be able to follow the tape and read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question to put to Mr. Mundis, first of all: Was this video admitted in what was called the Vukovar 3 trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would need to check our records on that, Mr. President. Perhaps if Dr. Seselj has any comments, I can come back to you in just a moment on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Second question, the interview of Mr. Sljivancanin addresses the question of the volunteers and he says on several occasions that these people are fighting side by side. These are the words he uses. Under the orders of the JNA, this is what he says. As far as he is concerned, these volunteers are placed under the command of the JNA. Right at the beginning of the report it -- he also seems to indicate that it is the army of Yugoslavia which is present. So, Mr. Seselj, your comments on this footage, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that this videotape should be admitted but I have to express -- to say I'm sorry that it was cut off when it seemed to be the most interesting. After the statement of the then Major Sljvancanin and now colonel, we see a mass of soldiers and that's what I was most interested in seeing, whereas they cut it off there. So that's the problem with these very, very brief excerpts, because you could see a large group of soldiers towards the end and it would have been very interesting to see and if the Prosecution can continue the footage for some 10 to 15 seconds and not to exert censorship of the portion of the tape that might be the most relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we give this an exhibit number, could you tell us whether this video has already been admitted in the Radic, Sljvancanin and Mrksic trial, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It was not admitted in that trial according to our records, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we shall admit it now. Can we have an exhibit number, please, registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next exhibit number shall be P00291. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you instruct the Prosecutor to state his views. Was this footage tendered in the other trial, or did they not tender it at all? Was it tendered and rejected by the Trial Chamber there or was it or not? That would be an interesting point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is strange, because that was exactly the question that came to mind. Mr. Mundis, as far as you know, this video which has to do with one of the accused in the Vukovar trial, had it been adduced or not? Had it not been admitted? Had it been adduced by the Prosecution or the Defence or what happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps noting the time, we could take our recess at this point in time and I will endeavour to provide an answer to that question once we recommence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break I would like to read out an oral decision which is important. I shall read it in closed session, because it is both urgent and important. Registrar, can we move into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I believe we have now reached the video clip bearing number 6025.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. And this tape was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 19 September 2003. This apparently also comes from TV Novi Sad, and this clip --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. I have an objection. Mr. Mundis promised before the break to explain to us whether the previous clip was tendered in the Mrksic, Sljvancanin, Radic case and rejected by the Chamber or whether it was not tendered by the Prosecution at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was precisely about to ask him that, but he's first going to finish the presentation of this video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me -- let me just address that point before this tape, since it's come up. Mr. Mussemeyer is attempting to locate that information definitively. We on some occasions have the same videotape under different numbers because we received it from different sources, and so what we're trying to determine is that -- a definitive answer whether that tape was tendered into evidence or not, and if it was tendered, by whom and what was the decision of the Vukovar 3 Trial Chamber, because clearly the numbered version that we had was not admitted in that case. So I would expect we would have an answer to that question as soon as Mr. Mussemeyer returns to the courtroom. So the answer will come in the physical presence of Mr. Mussemeyer returning to the courtroom. So I don't have any information on that point until my colleague returns. So I would suggest that we just continue. I will get the answer. If I don't have the answer today, I will have the answer on Tuesday of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So again for the record this is 65 ter number 6025. The old number was -- the old 65 ter number was 0729. This clip runs approximately one minute.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] [No interpretation]. Reporter: And that we have to fight now in the present time to create a new country and a new land where people are going to recognise us, respect us, love us, and where we shall serve the interests of the people. "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, apparently there was a problem. There was no interpretation into English. Is that so? So we'll have to start again. [In English] Start again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: Attitude, dignity, courage. "Sljivancanin: All the soldiers of Operations Group South, especially those of the Guards Brigade, all the volunteers, then the units of the Vukovar Territorial Defence, the Leva Supoderica detachment that participated side by side with our soldiers and were under the single command of the Yugoslav People's Army acted with true heroism and valour. We would not have been able to carry out this task without these volunteers. The city of Vukovar Territorial Defence detachment in which, unfortunately, there were fewer than we expected but the few that were there were the right ones and they were courageous and they helped and they helped us a lot. And that's why I still definitely think and I keep pointing out that we really are the Yugoslav People's Army, that we are the people's army, that we cannot do without the people and that we have to fight now to create a new country and a new land where people are going to recognise us, respect, us, love us, and where we shall serve of the interests of the people."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the officer, Sljvancanin, says two things that struck me. First, he recalled that this operation was conducted under the authority of the South Operational Group. The second thing that he pointed out relating to the volunteers, he said that everybody acted under the unified command or the single command of the JNA. That's what he said. Your comments, Mr. Seselj, and then we'll hear the Prosecutor -- or let's start with the Prosecutor, since Mr. Mussemeyer is back in the courtroom. The previous video clip and this one, were they admitted in the Vukovar trial or not, or were they not presented to be adduced into evidence, or was the tendering sought and rejected?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect to the tape that was shown prior to the break which was admitted in this case as P291, that interview of Major Sljvancanin was not tendered into evidence and consequently, obviously, was not admitted in that case. I will make a similar inquiry with respect to the clip we've just looked at, 6025.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with the previous clip, I think it's very important, Judges, sirs, to point out that this is evidently exculpatory material for Mr. Sljvancanin and for all the accused in the case, Mrksic and Radic also. It's exculpatory for me also. It's very important to say that the OTP had this at their disposal but they did not tender it in the case where the Vukovar 3 were tried. It is evident from this that before the liberation of Vukovar nobody had the intention of shooting prisoners. He says for them to surrender, for everything to be peaceful, and that is my case, that the order to shoot the prisoners came after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm so sorry for interrupting you, Mr. Seselj, but as you know, you are not presently testifying. We only ask comments, technical comments from you regarding the videotape. Don't go to the merits, which is what you're presently doing in two ways, because you now speak about the other case, but that other case does not concern you. It is for the others to raise such issues if this is indeed in their interest. Now, you say it's exculpatory. Well, that's what you say, but you will have an opportunity to prove this through your own witnesses and when you testify in person. Therefore, at this stage we cannot make any legal findings because you're not testifying. You are merely making comments, technical comments at that, on a tape which we have just been viewing. And you can say, just as I do, that Mr. Sljvancanin is saying that volunteers operated under the single command without any further comment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm interested in principle in all the cases before this Tribunal. They all concern me, especially those that touch on my case, because I'm accused of participating in a joint criminal enterprise. That's the first point. The second point is the following: It's an international scandal that the previous clip was not shown in the Mrksic, Radic, Sljvancanin case, an international scandal. And my third point and last one is that I hope the OTP is not going to ask me for a fee because they offered -- or, rather, they tendered these clips which are very important to my case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you do not oppose the admission of this video clip number 6025. I want a number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number P00292. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P292. Very well. Next clip, Mr. Mundis. It is the 4143, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, Mr. President. The next tape bears 65 ter number 4143. The old 65 ter number was 0298. Again, the source of this was the B-92 documentary "Vukovar, the Final Cut." This documentary was produced by B-92 in 2006 and was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 3rd of March, 2006. This clip runs 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Blazevic: In a bullet-proof vest with a beard. These are all butchers and murderers. This was all staged. The person from the television came to tell him what to do. This was filmed seven times. "Unknown man: I was in the cellar all the time. "Journalist: Is it true what they're saying? "Milivojevic: These are murderers and butchers. Lie down. There's nothing more to discuss. "Blazevic: I wanted to be filmed because it would be evidence that I was still alive."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Could it be shown again because it was very fast. In the beginning one has the impression that there are two pictures next to one another. It's not very long. Maybe we can see it again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Blazevic: The tall guy in the bullet-proof vest with the helmet who shouted, 'Get down, those are murderers and butchers.' This was part of the scenario. The television director talked to him. It was shot seven times. He told him what to say. This guy didn't know how to repeat what he said and then he told him, 'Go and say whatever you want.' "Unknown man: I haven't been anywhere. I haven't been anywhere. I was in the basement the whole time. I haven't been anywhere. "Journalist: Is it true what they're saying? "Milivojevic: That's a lie. A downright lie. Those are murderers and butchers. Get down. Get down for Christ's sake. We don't have anything to talk to you about. "Blazevic: I wanted that television crew to film me because if they did film me, well, others would then see that I was alive."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very difficult to understand this video clip. However, at one point in time we hear the name of Topola being mentioned. Yes, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Seselj, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me or not, Judges, sirs, I have never seen Topola in my life. Here this soldier is introduced as Topola, but let me draw your attention to one point. He had white belts on both sides and this means that he belonged to the military police. He had white straps and white straps were worn exclusively by the military police and it was the military police that was in charge of guarding the prisoners. The identity of this man has to be established. I don't know who he is. Evidently this is about prisoners whom somebody is guarding and he told them to lie down while he was guarding them. If there's only one man guarding them, it's easier for him to guard them while they're lying down otherwise one of them might escape. We don't see any arrests being made here. We don't see any torture but we hear what the soldier says that the people who have been taken prisoner are murderers and butchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has discussed the issue. It is hard to understand this video clip. Therefore, the Trial Chamber will ask the registrar to give us a MFI number, because we have nothing to admit this document definitively. So this can be submitted again by one or the other party if they so wish. So a MFI number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This will be P00293, marked for identification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we have finished the first chapter. We now can move on to the second theme, can't we.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President. The second theme which the Prosecution short-handedly indicated as Vojislav Seselj and his Vojvodas on the front lines. The first clip is P16 marked for identification. This tape was received by the Croatian government in response to a request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor. It was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 30 March 2004. The tape that we received was a compilation of various reports. The date of this broadcast is indicated on the tape as being July -- or, sorry, 7 November 1991. That's 7 November 1991. And again, I believe the source of this tape, although it came from the Croatian government, was television Novi Sad, and this was P16, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] VS: Those are our volunteers who make part of the Territorial Defence. We haven't got any units of our own here. All the people here are our people. All the units here are our units, and of course those who have come here voluntarily to fight. They know why they are here and what they're fighting for and they don't need to be persuaded to fight because they themselves wanted to do so and therefore one should not be surprised by their courage. "J: How significant is the liberation of Vukovar for Serbia and the Serbian people? "VS: It's of exceptional significance, exceptional significance. This is the most powerful Ustasha stronghold. Once Vukovar is taken, the Ustasha have no chance of saving either Osijek or Vinkovci. There is nothing to stop our forces. Vukovar is the key line that needs to be broken through, that needs to be captured and then there will be nothing the Ustasha can do. The Ustashas know that if Vukovar falls here, if Slunj falls in the Serbian Krajina, then Tudjman's Ustasha regime in Zagreb will fall too. And that is why this battle here is a decisive one."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll play the clip again because right from the beginning -- at the beginning, rather, there was an insignia which might be relevant. So can we have the clip again. And once we say -- when we say stop, please stop the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] VS: These are our own volunteers who are part of the Territorial Defence."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I noticed this insignia on the beret of the individual standing on the right of the picture. We've seen that insignia before. Unless I'm mistaken, it's an insignia we can also find on the helmet worn by Mr. Seselj during the interview. Therefore, my question is what is the meaning of this insignia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should maybe play it again, because the insignia is hidden by the logo of the Tribunal. So we'll play it again and say stop and then you stop immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. The individual who is standing to the right of the picture has a beret with a cross-shaped insignia. It's the same cross we saw on the previous beret. And then Mr. Seselj told us it was probably a foreign beret with an insignia added. But here we see it very clearly. We see the cross very clearly on this beret. It's the same as the one we saw earlier on on the other beret. Mr. Seselj will probably have something to say about this. Let me remind you that this exhibit has already received a MFI number, P16. Mr. Seselj, your comments.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First I have to tell you that the Yugoslav People's Army did not have such berets before 1990, except for the parachute units, but the OTP should have at their disposal a large number of clips of the Territorial Defence from the western part of the Serbian Krajina, the Knin Krajina. Their members wore such a coat of arms. It's a cross with four Cyrillic letters S, but they turned them round so they were not facing away from the cross but towards the cross, because they represent four letters S which stands for only -- only harmony or brotherhood will save the Serbs. We should see what else there is apart from the cross on this insignia. I don't think this was common in Vukovar. I think only one or two men had such insignia in Vukovar. Most of them wore the old Serbian coats of arms, the so-called cockades and these were made of metal. On my helmet you couldn't see that. You could see traces of the red five-pointed star which I scraped off with a bayonet but I was unable to scrape it off completely and you can see that on the helmet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Irrespective of all this, do you have any other comments about the rest of the video?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just draw your attention to the following: All the volunteers around me are very neat and tidy with full military uniforms on and helmets on. I think I should draw your attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The Trial Chamber has decided that this exhibit that bore the MFI number P16 is now going to be P16 without MFI. Let's move on to the following video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I should also indicate, perhaps I should have done this earlier, if -- in light of the reference Your Honour just made to the ICTY logo, if you toggle to the e-court button on your monitors the videos will be shown without the ICTY logo and the image is a little bit clearer, actually, than if you were to toggle to the video button on the switch.
