So the e-court, for the benefit of everyone in here, the e-court channel will give you the best imagery of the videos. The next video is -- has already been admitted into evidence under numbers P60 and P185. This tape was received from the Croatian government on 31 July 2001, apparently was recorded by TV Benkovac, and there are references on this tape to the date being 23 November 1991. This is P60 and P185.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] N: During the inspection of combat positions, Captain Dragan came along. Let's see what looked like when they met. "CD: What joint combat? We sent a dispatch to the president.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is unable to distinguish any words in the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] JNAO: He's not here. No. No. No. He went over there. He's -- Uzelac, where is the guy? "VS: Captain Dragan objected because he was against the Chetniks. "UM: Mr. President, come over to this side a little bit. Commander, come here. We won't argue. We won't argue. We want to create the Serb army. "CD: I've just come to say hello. I'm heading for Belgrade. "CD: But you agree that I wouldn't -- "CD: Babic is a hero. I'm just a workout instructor. "VS: You got involved in politics, man, and you shouldn't have. If the conflict occurred -- "CD: Sir, but I'm telling the truth and must I not say what I think the truth is? "VS: No, you must not until the war is over because if this truth is useful in wartime, you mustn't say it. "VS: There are other battlefields for Captain Dragan in Western Slavonia. He came here and he's done a lot here. "CD: No, you have Milan Babic here. He's your hero. "VS: Today you're turning the army against the Krajina prime minister. He's the prime minister, no matter what he's like. "CD: He's a coward, a coward, a traitor who broke up our unit, who broke up Knin. "VS: You're the one who's breaking it up. You're breaking the battle field right here and you shouldn't have come. You're the one who is breaking up the battlefield. "JNAO: Please, since this is my territory I would prefer it if you didn't talk about that here. No, this is not the place to discuss that I came to make peace with Milan Babic and Milan Martic. You shouldn't have talked about it here at all. "CD: Who asks the -- who's asking the people? Who's asking the people? "L: This influences morale. "CD: No, but Babic Vojvoda and others pointed out -- "VS: You got involved in a conflict that you shouldn't have interfered in. Ask Babic. Since Babic is the prime minister anybody who don't like it can leave the Krajina. We are the army but the people decide which authorities, which government is good and which is not. You came here to help not to interfere. In a state of war you cannot change the government. The government has to be changed by elections. People don't -- don't interfere in this."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video clip has already been admitted with the following numbers: P60 and P185. The least you can say is that there is a very lively discussion here between Mr. Seselj and the other persons, especially the individual wearing a red beret and an insignia with three stars at the front of his uniform, a man with the white hair. Now, what is the context of this video? It's not really something you can say just watching it. Mr. Seselj, you were there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This short man is Dragan Vasiljovic, also known as Captain Dragan. I'm sure that you've heard of him. At least the OTP knows the name. He bears the same insignia that the Judge Harhoff pointed to. This is a cross with four Ss, an insignia that was made for the Territorial Defence for Knin Krajina, and there were samples spread all over the place. Some were even worn -- worn in Belgrade. Second of all, this was taken two or three days after the fall of Vukovar. We need a date here. The Prosecution has not provided us with a date. This is the moment when I arrived in Knin in order to prevent the rebellion of the army against the Srpska Krajina government which was being organised by Captain Dragan. After that, Captain Dragan left Krajina. I have to explain the background of the footage otherwise we can ask about the relevance of this footage. On the 20th of November in Banja Luka, I received a message from Milan Babic to arrive urgently in Knin and to help him fight Captain Dragan. If you don't need the context of this footage, then you don't need the footage either, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, here you're addressing the substance of this video. We'll come back to that later. What's relevant is that you were there, Captain Dragan was there, there was a discussion. There's obviously disagreement between you. As for the rest, we'll deal with it later. You very probably will have the opportunity to deal with that again and talk to us about Captain Dragan. Furthermore, this video clip has already been admitted. Let's move on to the following one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I have to provide a comment. I don't have to deal with Captain Dragan because we did not have any contacts and there is nothing in my indictment speaking about the western part of Serbian Krajina. Second of all, if you're not interested in the context of this footage, then the question of the relevance of this footage arises. How can this footage be irrelevant for the fact that I am much higher than Captain Dragan and that the uniform fits me much better. As a military figure, I -- I looked very becoming. How else would it be relevant if you don't want me to give you the context? If you need the context, then it can be put in two short sentences. Obviously Captain Dragan had his own unit there. He did not obey the authority of the civilian government or the military government, and he had to be expelled from Krajina. After he was once expelled, he returned in order to rebel against the government of Serbian Krajina. That is the context and I'm opposing his attempts to stage up a putsch. If you don't need the context then I really don't know why you would need the footage at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've reminded us of the context. Very well. Let's move on to the following video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next tape or the next clip bears 65 ter number 6013. The old number was 3155. The date of this footage is 18 November -- I believe this might be a typo. It says 1992. The particular report was shown on Yutel and was produced by SRT Knin. The Prosecution received this tape on 28 September 2006. This is 65 ter number 6013.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Journalist: The appearance of the president of the Serbian Radical Party, Dr. Vojislav Seselj, who commands great respect in Vukovar, was met with a storm of applause. "Seselj: Serbian brothers and Serbian sisters, we have reached the anniversary of the freedom of heroic Serbian Vukovar. A year --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not getting any interpretation. Okay. Let's start again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Journalist: The appearance of the president of the Serbian Radical Party, Dr. Vojislav Seselj, who commands great respect in Vukovar, was met with a storm of applause. "Seselj: Serbian brothers and sisters, we have reached the anniversary of the freedom of heroic Serbian Vukovar, a year of Serbian pride, unity, and dignity, but also a year of great sorrow for heroes who have built their lives into the foundations of heroic Vukovar, who have fallen for its freedom. As in any other war, in this liberation war of the western Serbs, the best ones among us, the bravest, the most heroic ones have fallen, the ones whom Serbdom held as most precious have fallen. Today when most of Serbian Slavonia, Serbian Baranja, Serbian Western Srem, Serbian Dalmatia, Lika, Banija, and Kordun, Western Slavonia, when most of them are free we, the Serbs, have a reason to be proud. Big powers have pressed us from all sides. All the enemies of Serbdom have joined together in recent months to see us destroyed. It is clear to them, the main source of our strength is Serbia, and they would like to break the backbone of Serbia. They block her, introduce sanctions and surround her from all sides. They would like to see Serbia fall to her knees and then to be left adrift to tender mercies of our traditional enemies. But Serbia's backbone cannot be broken. Serbia cannot be forced to her knees, and Serbia will never leave you in the cold. She will never let the Republic of Serbian Krajina or Republika Srpska down. War is not a choice of us Serbs. We did not ask for this war either and we did not want it, but there is something that is more valuable and is more illustrious than peace - that is freedom and democracy. "We will not let somebody commit genocide over the Serbian people again. We will not let the Serbs, their hands tied be led to pitfalls, to slaughterhouses, to execution sites. This time the Serb has readily met with his enemies, have prepared for him, and this time the Serb has persisted. He knew how to protect and how to liberate what is his. "We the Serbs want peace. From all the neighbouring peoples, we are the one which cares about peace the most because we have suffered the greatest number of casualties in this 20th century in liberation wars. But we, the Serbs, will not give what belongs to us. We live free and proud in traditional Serbian lands. We are not giving even an inch of these lands. We do want peace but we also want to have demarcation lines drawn up between ourselves, the Croats and other Serb haters. Definitely we will not go into a united and common state ever again. We do want peace, but we do not want to negotiate while the sanctions are in place, while the blockade is in place. There must be no talks with anybody while our hands are tied. Serbian brothers and Serbian sisters, what worries you the most is the fact that this country is being led by the treacherous government of Milan Panic. "Audience: That's right. That's right. "Seselj: Milan Panic has been planted among the Serbian people as a trick played on them, but he will not survive for long. He will not realise any of his treacherous ideas because we, the Serbs, will not let him do that, not the Serbs from Serbia, not the Serbs from Montenegro, not the Serbs from Serbian Krajina or the Serbs from Republika Srpska. His days are numbered. "Audience: That's right. "Seselj: And this winter no Serb, no Serbian child, must be cold, and nobody must be hungry. We are capable of providing that, and we will take care of the rest together with joint forces. We shall resist all trials. Nobody can take Serbian Krajina away from us, so as long as you are united and in accord with each other and so long as Serbia is ready to give you a helping hand, and it will be ready evermore, Serbian Krajina remains ours. Goodbye with the traditional Serbian greeting, 'Serbia will be eternal as long as her children are faithful.' Goodbye."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. In the summary I have here, the Prosecutor stated that Milan Lancuzanin, aka Kameni, was standing next to Mr. Seselj. I've never seen Mr. Kameni, so I do not know whether he was standing behind Mr. Seselj or not. Apparently he must have been there, because that's been specified here by the Prosecution. For the rest, we have a speech delivered on the anniversary of the fall of Vukovar, on the first anniversary of the fall of Vukovar. Mr. Seselj, do you have any objections against the admission of this video? After all, it's a speech of yours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Mr. President, I would like to object to your comment. You said apparently Kameni was there, because that's what the OTP put in their description, and I guarantee to you that not even the Prosecutor can point to Kameni in this footage. If you can play the footage again and ask the Prosecutor to point to Kameni to you, you will see what happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now going to turn to the Prosecution. Why did you say here in the summary that Kameni was standing next or behind Mr. Seselj whilst Mr. Seselj was delivering his speech?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if the tape can be played again, at the beginning I believe that there is a very short part at the beginning of the tape where Kameni is visible on this tape, and I would ask that the first -- beginning of this tape be shown again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think to see him just in front of Dr. Seselj when they are marching. There is a person with blonde hair, and it seems to me Milan Lancuzanin. If we can see it again, and Mr. Seselj can check this, it would be great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, the Prosecutor tells us that Mr. Kameni's the one here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, your experiment is successful. The Prosecutor indeed did recognise Kameni, and it is Kameni.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is indeed Kameni. Now, with respect to the admission of this video, do you have any observations?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object because of the technical quality, and also this is not an integral footage. I really enjoyed listening to myself delivering this speech such a long time ago and that's why I'm really sorry that I could not see the whole footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number P00294. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to the following video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Next clip, Mr. President and Your Honours, has already been admitted into evidence as P56, P56. This is a clip that runs about 35 seconds from a documentary series entitled "Pictures Of Words And Hate, Year Two." It was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 6th of November, 2002. This is P56.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] UM: Shoot -- shoot at the log. Shoot at the log. "MB: I am the president of the Serbian Radical Party [as interpreted]. We actually control all the accesses to the city and all exits from it, too, and we control approximately 75 per cent of the city."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video was admitted. It was shot during a combat operation because we can hear the shots. Mr. Seselj, do you have any comments?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to let you know that these were local members of the Serbian Radical Party. All these people were from Bijeljina. They were fighting against the Muslim paramilitary formations and this is all I would like to draw your attention to. And you can see that they don't wear complete uniforms of the JNA. They wear whatever they could get hold of to look, to resemble soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next video footage, please, because this video has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip actually is two clips. It's also been previously admitted into evidence. This is P30, P30. This is raw footage from the Laura Silber interview with Dr. Seselj for "The Death of Yugoslavia" BBC series. The first clip runs 4 minutes and 17 seconds. The second clip runs 1 minute and 27 seconds. Again, this has previously been admitted under Exhibit number P30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] LS: Were your units in Zvornik in 1992, either you or your units. "VS: Yes, our volunteers were in Zvornik. Arkan's volunteers participated, too, as did another formation of a certain Zuca who was under the command of the police and who is now being tried for war crimes. "LS: And how did all of this come about? How did you decide to go? Did you get an order from Belgrade? Did you get a request from Srpska? How did everything come about? "VS: Yes. We never received any orders. These were always requests. Milosevic would ask us or Radmilo Bogdanovic would ask us. Some general would ask us, Domazetovic, for example, or somebody else. They would say they need so many volunteers for this and that location and we would gather that many volunteers. When they say they need the most experienced ones, we send the most experienced one. When they say they could also use those with not much experience because it is nothing dangerous, then we send such people. It was always like that. "LS: And who then asked you to send your units? "VS: In 1992, in May, I began having meetings with Milosevic on a more regular basis and back then it was always Milosevic himself who asked for volunteers to be sent out. I mean, one didn't have to convince us very much. We took this as our duty, our responsibility except when it came to the deployment where the most capable and the most disciplined men would be. They -- "LS: Could you then tell us about one such conversation regarding any places where you went or where you sent your units. How would the conversations with President Milosevic go regarding that? "VS: Those were very -- were always quick agreements. For example, when Tudjman attacked Pocitelj, Divoselo and Citluk in 1993. Milosevic had some sorts of agreements with him about that but it seems that Tudjman did not keep his end of the deal. They had some underhand dealings there, Milosevic was disappointed by Tudjman's actions and therefore decided at the last minute to send volunteers there. He called me and I went to him right away. He said 3 or 4.000 volunteers need to be sent to Divoselo, Citluk and Pocitelj. We had 3 to 5.000 volunteers within two days and Arkan brought along with him around 300 more. They were sent out from Belgrade in literally two days. There were never any problems with that. We would agree on this very quickly. This was always agreed upon in a few words. We need to go. Let's go. "LS: If you could concretely tell us how it came about that you went to Zvornik. How did all of this come about. "VS: You see, our volunteers were involved when the Zvornik operation began, but only while the fighting lasted. They withdrew as soon as the fighting ceased. However, some other forces under the control of the Serbian police stayed behind and as soon as the operation was finished, they began looting. They looted everything they could get their hands on. They even stole from Serbs they came across. They were not checking anything. They were all the same, stealing cars, foreign currency, and so on. That caused great discontent among the people. What was also happening there during the war and apart from everything else was, you know, a mass movement of people. All the Serbs who remained under Muslim control tried frantically to cross to the Serb side. All the Muslims under Serb control frantically and instinctively tried to cross over to the Muslim side. Well, the Serbs let all the Muslims go but the Muslims did not let all the Serbs go. It was then that the myth about ethnic cleansing came about. I cannot say it did not happen anywhere but I can claim that it was never done in a systematic and organised manner by the Serbs. Sometimes this was more organised here in Belgrade in order to set up Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] LS: And if you could describe to us why it was actually important for the Serbs. If you could tell us how things went when you left to Zvornik. Who told you to go? How did it all happen? "VS: You see, in May 1992 Milosevic definitely takes over the absolute control of the Yugoslav People's Army. It was then that the new constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was adopted and he formally and actually became the main man in the country. The man who made all the decisions. The Zvornik operation was planned in Belgrade. Bosnian Serb forces participated in it and they were the most numerous ones. However, the special units and the units most eager to fight came from this side. Those were the very police units, the so-called Red Berets. Those were the police units, the so-called Red Berets. Thy are special units of the Serbian State Security Service. There were volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, Arkan's volunteers and there was also a smaller volunteer unit also under the control of the police. The army did not participate much in this operation. They mainly provided artillery support when needed. It took a long time to plan, to prepare the operation so there was no nervousness or calls such as, Come on, we need this or that urgently. Everything was well organised and well executed up until the hostilities ceased. Afterwards when the looting began, no one could control it any more."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We've seen this portion of the footage, 4 minutes 17 seconds, 1 minute and 20 seconds. This footage has already been admitted under Exhibit number P30. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My observation and objection is that the complete tape was not shown of Laura Silber, because things have been pulled out of context. As far as I remember, I described how the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party set out for Zvornik from Belgrade and that they were trained and armed in Bubanj Potok, that they set out in buses and so on and so forth. So whether in that interview or in some other interview, however, this other interview is in the possession of the Prosecutor as well and I think it was brought up in another trial. I referred to a man who commanded the police volunteers, and that was Vojislav Jekic who was the commander of the police either in Zvornik, chief of police either in Zvornik or in Loznica, and he took part in the operation to liberate a place called Kula Grad above Zvornik. So just one objection and that is that the entire tape of this conversation and interview were not shown so that we could clarify many other points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your comments are on the transcript. The Trial Chamber will bear all of this in mind, of course. We shall now move on to the next one, which is 6055.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, 65 ter number 6055 bearing old 65 ter number 0764 is the next clip. It runs approximately 3 minutes and 50 seconds. This was a compilation videotape concerning media coverage of Milan Martic. It was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 3 January 2002 from the Croatian government and includes some video footage taken by Serbian Krajina television. This is 65 ter number 6055.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: One of the reasons of our visit was the successful action a few days ago in which 16 Ustashas were liquidated. In connection with this, the commander of the Republic of Serbian Krajina army Main Staff, General Mile Novakovic, and Minister Milan Martic visited the Serbian volunteers. General Novakovic congratulated the soldiers on the successful action, stressed that their unit could serve as a model to all those defending Serbdom. "Novakovic: The Serbian army's Main Staff particularly values the Serbian volunteers who have come to these western Serbian states to defend them, to defend and protect both this people and this territory of ours. We value you because we know that you have not come here to fight for the sake of appearances, in order to seek glory for yourselves in war or for any selfish, egoistical reasons but you have come to fight for the freedom and honour of the Serbian people. "Reporter: Vojvoda Jovo Ostojic, who leads this elite unit, appealed to all Serbs who have not done so to join the defensive ranks because Serbdom is not defended either in Belgrade or in Knin but everywhere where Serbs have been attacked. The Serbian volunteers include members of all parties but at this moment none of them are interested in politics and they're all fighting under the unified command of the Republic of Serbian Krajina army Main Staff. "Ostojic: The motto of our fighters is patriotism and freedom for the Serbian people and nothing else. We want to defend the Serbian lands, to defend Serbian children and Serbian mothers, and to counter the Ustasha devils militarily and heroically. And I would send this message out to them: Let them leave the innocent alone. Let them be men and let them stand on the battlefield and choose their own weapons. We are ready. It makes me very sad. We -- there are Croatian women and children here and not a hair on anyone's head should be harmed, but they stick our children on knives and slaughter our -- "Reporter: The oldest soldier in Jovo Ostojic's unit is over 60 years old and that is why he is called Solunac, the Salonika front veteran. "Djeric: They call me Solunac. I am Dusan Djeric from Sombor. "Reporter: And tell me how old are you. "Djeric: I'm 63 years old. "Reporter: And how long have you been in this unit? "Djeric: From the start. I have been in this unit since it was formed. "Reporter: You've seen many fronts. "Djeric: Many fronts. And I'm very proud of my commander, Zuca from Apatin. So far we have completed every assignment we were given. We are still planning, and I am therefore telling those who stand in our way, just as we have completed assignments up to now, I hope that we will complete the next assignment that we are planning still better. "Reporter: At the end the Serbian volunteers sent greetings to Serbs in the Krajina. So as not to send greetings one at a time because there are many of them, they sang it together as true Serbs do. "Male voices: From our victory the sun of freedom rises, from our victory."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, any comments?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite sure that the Prosecutor gave us the date when this video was taped, but I could identify myself. It was 1993, when the Croats destroyed three Serbian villages and killed all the civilian population in them. They are Citluk, Pocitelj, and Divoselo, and that was when we sent a large number of volunteers out from Serbia to help out. And most of these volunteers shown here are from the Serbian Radical Party, and this is the Chetnik Vojvoda, Ostojic. I proclaimed him a Chetnik Vojvoda myself. Once again the question of relevance arises. As far as I'm concerned, this is inculpatory -- exculpatory, interpreter's correction exculpatory material for me because Vojvoda Ostojic says what the conduct should be toward civilians on the enemy side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number P00295.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to draw your attention to. I think I have to do that. Look how well dressed all these volunteers are. There are young girls among them, young women, and you can see some with beards but the beards are properly clipped, large beards like Fidel Castro but well-kept. So regardless of the fact that he was a Communist, Fidel Castro, it's a fine example for us because he's fighting the Americans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Registrar, can we have a new exhibit number, because this was not recorded on line 17. I need to look at the screen and listen all at once. It's difficult, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit number P00295, Your Honours. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, next piece of footage, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next video clip, Your Honours, bears 65 ter number 6069. The old 65 ter number was 0759. This is material that was received from the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina pursuant to a request for assistance. This shows or this material comes from Srpska Radio Televizija. This is on or after 13 May 1995. This is clip 6 -- PT -- 65 ter number 6069.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Announcer: Dr. Vojislav Seselj, chairman of the Serbian Radical Party, visited Sarajevo and going around the streets of Sarajevo he visited the front lines. Dr. Vojislav Seselj stressed again that the Serbs east of the Drina River think and empathise with the people in Republika Srpska and support the liberation struggle of the Serbian people in these territories. "VS: I am very happy, first of all, because of the very, very high morale of the Serbian fighters to end this liberation war with complete Serbian victory. And today I am more than ever convinced that the whole of Sarajevo will finally be Serbian. We are here now in Serbian Hadzici, Hadzici which from the first day of the war resisted violent Muslim attacks but also Hadzici which triumphed in this war which managed to save everything that is Serbian. Even the entire Mount Igman was liberated but Muslims returned afterwards under UNPROFOR aegis with which UNPROFOR actually showed whose side it was on in this war. Igman will remain Serbian. I am convinced of that because of the strength of the Serbian fighters, because of their faith in the Serbian cause, and because of their faith in a Greater Serbia. Here the people created a state which is strong, functions well and notwithstanding poverty, the hard life the Serbian people of Republika Srpska will be triumphant. They will be victorious. The destiny of Serbian Krajina is most of all linked to Republika Srpska not to those rulers from Dedinje. The future of the Serbian Krajina is in the unification with Republika Srpska, unification now. Unification tomorrow, straight away. "Announcer: At the end of his visit to Srpska Sarajevo, Dr. Vojislav Seselj told citizens and combatants to endure in the righteous struggle and that Serb radicals will help as much as they're able to, that the Serbian people in Republika Srpska achieve final victory and freedom."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, any comments?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no special observations to make except that this is footage from 1995, so I don't know how you're going to incorporate this unbelievably into the indictment. Otherwise, I'm proud. This is my visit to Serbian Sarajevo in May 1995, and that's what it says roughly in the information provided by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, this is a visit by Mr. Seselj in 1995. Clearly this is outside the scope of the indictment. What is the point of showing this video? What's the point of this, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, it shows that even after the indictment period it clearly shows Dr. Seselj with some of the volunteers. We would assert that visible in that videotape is -- along with Dr. Seselj is Branislav Gavrilovic, also known as Brne, one of the Vojvodas. So it would certainly demonstrate that even after the indictment period Dr. Seselj was associating with Vojvodas and some of the volunteers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, by the Dayton Accords, according to the Dayton Accords, a lot of territory of Serbian Sarajevo had to be handed over including Ilidza, Vogosca, Ilijas, and so on. Branislav Gavrilovic, Brne, moved to Serbia. He didn't have anywhere to live because he comes from those parts. And when I became president of the Zemun municipality, the first thing I did was to employ him in the service for security of the Zemun municipality, to give him a livelihood, a means of livelihood for himself and his family, and then from Zemun municipality he was given a flat in Belgrade. So when did I challenge having seen him. Then he was employed in the security service of the Serbian Radical Party later on, so of course I saw him. Of course I met with him but what has that got to do with the period relevant to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Prosecution is saying that what is outside the scope of the indictment is this: You went to meet some volunteers. Do you feel that this video is useful to you in any way, because if it may seem useful and if everybody agrees, then there he's no reason why it should not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as a politician this is very useful because it's going to be shown on Serbian television this evening, but I don't know how legally relevant it is. So I'm not opposed to it. I didn't visit the volunteers. These were Republika Srpska soldiers and we didn't have any volunteers there at that time at all. That's the fact of the matter and the Prosecution knows that after 1993, we couldn't send volunteers out anywhere because of the conflict with Milosevic's regime everything was blocked after 1993. So there are no traces of any volunteers being sent to any of the fronts from Serbia unless someone happened to swim across the Drina River and went to fight. There was no organised sending of volunteers any more. It was just not possible at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we shall admit it and see later on whether we value it in any way. For the time being it doesn't seem to be very useful. The Prosecution is asking to have it admitted and you have nothing against it notwithstanding its relevance, but insofar as volunteers are mentioned in this video, even if in 1995 there are no more volunteers, these are perhaps former volunteers. So I think we could spend a lot of time discussing this, but could we have an exhibit number, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P00296, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're now addressing another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is a topic which only includes one video clip at this point in time and that is 65 ter number 1836, bearing old 65 ter number 0763. This tape was received from Serbian television. We do not have information concerning the date that this video material was taken. The clip that we have loaded up runs about one and a half minutes long.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: Would that mean a bloodthirsty killing of civilians? "Seselj: Well, every war is bloodthirsty and this war has not been particularly bloodthirsty in comparison to other wars. This war has been less inhumane, less bloodthirsty in any case than the ones the Germans fought in this century "Reporter: And why the Muslims in particular? Why not the Croats? "Seselj: Because this time the Americans sided with the Muslims in this war. We cannot -- they intervened on the side of the Muslims and we have no reason to be attacking the Croats now. "Reporter: Let's take the example of Gorazde. What will -- what do you think will happen to Gorazde? "Seselj: I think there is no saving Gorazde, that Gorazde will fall into Serbian hands. "Reporter: And the Muslims in Gorazde? "Seselj: The Muslims from Gorazde will most likely go to Arizona, California, New Mexico, and so on ... under American protection. "Reporter: Will you allow this or will you try to prevent them? "Seselj: Whom should I prevent? "Reporter: The Muslims to leave. "Seselj: No, because they're very dear to the Americans. I think it is of mutual benefit the Americans cannot wait to take in those Muslims. The Muslims cannot wait to go to America and we cannot wait for something good to happen to the Muslims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So once again this seems to be outside the scope of the indictment, because US strikes are mentioned here and this comes after the indictment. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is rather problematic because once again it's not the entire tape. Here you can see that I'm hitting at the Americans, not the Muslims. So this footage, for it to be understandable at all, must be shown in total, and it's outside the relevant time. So it's just a manipulation on the part of the Prosecution. It's as if I am trying to say that I want the Muslims to be expelled from Gorazde, but you know that was already in 1994 when the Serbs had almost liberated Gorazde or just liberated Gorazde and then had NATO air-strikes against them and their operation had to stop. So that's that particular period. And they could have found footage where I threatened to USS 20 rockets to target American bases in Aviano. Perhaps that's on this part of the tape but they didn't want to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has decided orally not to admit this video. Let's move on to another topic, shall we?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be best, Mr. President and Your Honours, for the benefit of the record it could certainly be given an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We shall give it an MFI number in that case. The Trial Chamber does not admit this video as it stands so could we have a MFI number, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P00297 marked for identification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It might be better to have the break now and resume after the break. Let's have a 20-minute break and we'll finish after the break. We have still a few videos to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have an answer regarding the second video clip regarding Sljvancanin? Do you know whether it was submitted in the so-called Vukovar trial or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're still trying to determine if it was actually tendered. It was certainly not admitted into evidence in that trial along the same lines as the first video that we saw, the interview of Major Sljvancanin. Before -- Your Honours, before we proceed I do have a couple of issues that I would like to clarify or correct with respect to some of the videos we've seen earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Nothing's working right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you mind saying something so that we see whether we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. What I was saying is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead. It's good now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. What I was saying is that I need to correct two points with respect to videos that were shown earlier this morning, it's been drawn to my attention. The first issue concerns the videotape that had 65 ter number 6011. This was the videotape that had been previously marked P16 MFI. That clip that was shown this morning I have now been informed was a different clip from the same master tape, if you will, and the tape -- the clip that was shown this morning and which was admitted, therefore, actually should be assigned an entirely exhibit number. And the prior clip from that tape which was P16 MFI should remain as P16 MFI and perhaps we'll revisit that tape in the future with a witness or on another video day, but the clip that was admitted as P16 in fact was not the same as P16 MFI so I suggest that we revert to P16 MFI and leave that clip as that status and the new number be assigned to what was admitted as P16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, give us another number, a new number to replace P16. P16 remaining P16 MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That would be Exhibit number P00298. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the second issue concerns the tape that we just looked at, which was marked for identification P0297. Similarly, there were a number of clips that were taken from the original 65 ter number 1836, and as a result for the benefit of everyone's record-keeping the clip that has been MFI P00297, the 65 ter number for that should be 1836A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So 1836A instead of just 1836; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's go on -- move on. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President, but quite obviously I can't think as quickly as I used to think several years ago. I've become a little senile being in the detention unit. The light flashed on when Milan Martic is praising the volunteers, and a volunteer is mentioning a commander called Zuca from Sombor, and I think that was the motive for the Prosecution to put forward this footage, because the Zuca from Sombor is not the same Zuca as the one from Belgrade who had the Zuta Osa, Yellow Wasp formation. So if that was the intention of the Prosecution, that can't stand. The nickname Zuca is very frequent in Serbia and usually it is people who are very blonde who are given the name Zuca, because it comes from yellow, so blonde yellow hair. So that particular lamp didn't flash on straight away. It took me a while to realise why the Prosecution actually wanted to slip that in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has been recorded in the transcript, of course, and the Trial Chamber will factor this in. Now I think we can move on to the next chapter, JCE, and organisation of volunteers. Is that so, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. President. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6069. The old number was -- the old 65 ter number was 0759. This is another clip from Srpska Radio Televizija. The approximate date of this tape is 13 May 1995. This tape was obtained from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina pursuant to a request for assistance. And I should note that the issues being discussed on this tape relate directly to the indictment period notwithstanding the fact that the tape itself was filmed in May of 1995. So I want to indicate that at the beginning, because we would potentially have the same issue that the tape was made outside the indictment period, but there are references to events inside the indictment period. And this is 65 ter number 6069.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just note that 65 ter number 6069 was also the one that we saw for Exhibit P296.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this would be clip A, if you note in the full name in the column. A lot of the videotapes in order to reduce the amount of -- the length of the tapes were subsequently cut into various clips and this is -- this is in fact from the same original tape, but it is clip A as compared with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Clip B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Clip B which was P2696.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] VS: It is very much more difficult for us to send volunteers than it was in 1991, 1992, and 1993. When we sent volunteers back then we had good cooperation with Slobodan Milosevic. He gave us uniforms, weapons, buses. He put the whole barracks in Bubanj Potok at the disposal of the Serbian Radical Party, all the technical equipment that was needed and that worked much better. Because of Slobodan Milosevic's betrayal, the Serbian Radical Party is now facing great difficulties in sending and equipping volunteers. Our volunteers are now being sent to their assignments in civilian clothes, to wherever certain Serbian army commands invite them, mostly to the Serbian Krajina, the western part of Serbian Krajina, the scarcely populated areas where our help is most needed. And these volunteers pass through the corridor in buses across Banja Luka and so on. The Serbs living there are already familiar with this. We cannot talk about numbers, of course."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, we have once again come across the problem of incomplete footage and the mention of Slobodan Milosevic here is personalising a regime, but it's a very complex question and you can't draw any conclusions on the basis that have very brief excerpt out of context. You know during the conflict with Milosevic, whenever we speak about the regime we in fact mention his name, but there's nothing that we're talking about here because all these questions have been clear and clarified, but it would have been a good idea to see the entire footage and not this brief excerpt which in itself says nothing. Once again, a question of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This video clip mentions volunteers who were dispatched, the issue of weapons, ammunition, logistics, so there is a connection and we're going to give a number to this video clip. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit number P00299. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip to be shown has been admitted into evidence as P30. This is further or additional material from "The Death of Yugoslavia" production concerning the interview that Dr. Seselj gave to Laura Silber in early March 1995. Again, there are two clips in this exhibit. The first one runs a little bit longer than one minute. The second one runs a little bit less than one minute, and this has been admitted as P30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] LS: And when you got those weapons you said the regime gave the weapons to your party or volunteers. Was the political leadership and Milosevic informed about that or did you get it through the police? "VS: Milosevic knew about all of it. There's no doubt about that. Key people from the police at the time with whom we established cooperation were Radmilo Bogdanovic, Mihalj Kertes and others, Franko Simatovic, called Frenki, and so on who commanded the red berets later, and so on. Then from the General Staff we mostly worked with General Domazetovic, who at the time was the deputy chief of the General Staff and the head of the personnel administration, if I remember correctly. But we also had contacts with lower-ranking officers and so on. Depending on the need and depending on the situation our volunteers would come to Belgrade to Bubanj Potok barracks. There they would put on their uniforms. They would be issued weapons and buses and they would go where needed. And they were under the command of the Yugoslav People's Army as soon as the Yugoslav People's Army got involved in the conflict."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've seen this already, and a long discussion ensued. Do you have anything to add to that, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd just like to draw your attention to all the shortcomings, the fact that this footage was not shown in its entirety so that people could conclude that I wanted to include Milosevic in everything, whereas in fact the truth is that we're talking about cooperation with the JNA. So this is information that is trying to be put in here, and I'm just trying to involve Milosevic in the conflict and mention him with respect to the conflict but you must bear in mind the fact that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were very popular in Serbia. There was not a single institution, not a single patriotic individual who praised them as being disciplined soldiers and so on and so forth. Now we come across here with a problem of reduction and editing, subsequent editing of evidence. For example, the Prosecution has information from the book by a certain woman called Dobrila Glisic-Gajic and she was brought in as a witness in the Slobodan Milosevic trial. She was the Chef de Cabinet of Tomislav Simovic, the defence minister. Now, they did not incorporate a single piece of information from her book here. Why? Because she testified and said that Slobodan Milosevic attacked General Tomislav Simovic for congratulating the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party as being brave and well-disciplined. The Prosecution has that but it doesn't want to offer that information up. They are providing us with an edited version and not with everything they have in their possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if the Prosecutor does not want to tender this as evidence, you can do so later yourself. Let's move on to the next clip, clip E. That's the second part, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I, interpreter's correction I.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] LS: Can you describe the moment when you parted ways with Milosevic? "VS: When the Vance Plan was put forward in April 1993. Milosevic called me several times to come for talks at his office at the Serbian Presidency and also at the state villa at Poticeva Street and at the Sava Centre prior to the failed all-Serbian convention and so on. He tried to convince me but couldn't. This was when we practically parted ways. The rest was all about trying to patch up the rift. We too thought it possible for Milosevic to return to decisive national policy so we could give him another chance. All of this lasted until the Vance -- well, until the attempted coup in Banja Luka. Karadzic was also counting on that, on Milosevic coming back after all, on him making a break and not rushing headlong and following through with that policy. And don't forget, Milosevic always won the elections here on a national platform exclusively."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was listening to this and I was looking at Mr. Seselj, and there was one contextual element that escapes me totally. Sometime they said the attempted coup in Banja Luka and I don't know what was this is about but this can be seen in this video clip. Your comments, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any observations to make but if you want me to explain that putsch to you, I can, if you need the information. If not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have an opportunity to get back to that. Let's move to the next clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip has also been admitted into evidence as P63. This videotape which runs a little bit more than five minutes is apparently amateur videotape. We received this -- the Office of the Prosecutor received this tape on the 13th of December, 2002. The tape was apparently shot at the end of March 1995. This is P63.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] J: Vojislav Seselj is addressing the Serbs from Glina only four months before Operation Oluja started. "VS: Milosevic needed us both in 1991 and 1992. Besides, Slobodan Milosevic was helping the western Serbian countries at the time, Serbian Krajina as well as Republika Srpska. Serbian Krajina and Republika Srpska were established with his help. Besides, he gave us the Serbian radicals, weapons for 30.000 volunteers. We were sending off to almost all the battlefields where they were most needed. He also gave us buses, uniforms. He put the whole barracks in Bubanj Potok at the disposal of the Serbian Radical Party for the volunteers. We haven't forgotten that. And also in the first days after the battle in Borovo Selo, when we were transporting the weapons across the Danube to Eastern Slavonia on rafts by night, that weaponry we got from the police warehouses and Serbian Territorial Defence warehouses pursuant to Milosevic's order. "We returned Milosevic's favour and supported him when he was having a tough time, the toughest time. The Z-4 plan, the Zagreb-4, a humiliation for the Serbian people from the beginning. What does Zagreb have to do with us the Serbs? If this is a Z-4 plan, then it should be implemented in Zagreb. Let them tear and divide up Zagreb instead. No plan can be accepted by the Serbian side if it envisages integration of the Serbian Krajina into Croatia. Well, we the Serbian radicals have sent 3.500 volunteers to Western Lika near Citluk and Pocitelj. He will probably attack Western Slavonia if he decides to or perhaps Slunj to emerge with the 5th Corps, to link up with the 5th Corps if the Serbs do not destroy the 5th Corps before that. But if he strikes now, he should be given such a blow that he will never recover from it. Let's win back even what we did not manage to recover in 1991, and then complete liberating everything that is ours, Zadar, Karlobag, and finally to finish with Gospic we have special motives for that, to liberate Karlovac where the majority of the population has always been Serbian. To liberate all of Western Slavonia, all the way to Virovitica. There is no other way. We can trade, exchange territories, but always those of the same value. If Maslenica is so important to Tudjman, we'll give it to him and he can give us the Dubrovnik coast stretch, let's say. That's the only way we can exchange territories. We want Grubisno Polje. We want the whole of Pakrac. This is the only way smart politicians should negotiate territories. "Brother and sister Serbs, we the Serbs shall win. We cannot lose. We must not lose. What we manage to preserve as Serbia now shall always remain Serbian. If we lose even a bit of our territories now, that will never be Serbian again. Serbian Krajina is not a part of Croatia. Serbian Krajina shall never be Croatian. But we should immediately move towards the first phase of unification, the direct and immediate unification of Republika Srpska and Serbian Krajina into a single state, western Serbia with Banja Luka as its capital. We must not allow ourselves to be torn apart and divided by others. Serbia will exist for us as long as its children are loyal to her. Long live Greater Serbia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has already been admitted as P63. Do you have any comments, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no comments to make on this. I would repeat this speech today even though the Serbian Krajina is currently occupied by Croatia with the help of the Americans. It will never be Croatian. We will certainly liberate it one day. Neither this Hague Tribunal nor anybody else can stand in the way of us Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm so sorry. These are political statements that are not allowed here in this Tribunal. I'm ever so sorry, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Judge, I am being tried here exclusively for politics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe for the past, but not for the future, and these are statements for the future.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all the more reason for the OTP to extend their indictment and charge me with my intentions for the future. I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, let's finish now with the video clip number 6025.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The final videotape to be shown today, 65 ter number 6025 previously bore 65 ter number 0729. This clip runs a little bit less than four minutes. It was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 19 September 2003. This footage apparently originally came from or was broadcast on Braca Karic TV, that's BKTV. This is 65 ter number 6025.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Seselj: That's one thing. Another thing, as regards what is stated in the indictment, they're lying, and I'll prove it. In Hrtkovci I didn't call out the names of Croats who should be expelled, I read out a list of Croats from Hrtkovci who had gone to Croatia and were serving in the Ustasha National Guard Corps. There were no expulsions. And regarding my statements, I wasn't making them as someone in power but as someone from the opposition."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There is a second clip as part of this 65 ter number 6025.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Seselj: ... for someone who is used to working. "Journalist: Tell me, will you be watching television or using a computer? How will you write those books? "Seselj: I don't know if that's possible. I have yet to find out. I have a laptop. "Novinar: That's good for communication, too. "Seselj: One cannot communicate, the internet is certainly switched off. Whether it's possible to keep a laptop in the cell without being connected to the internet, that's another question. We will have to see if that's possible."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, why show us this second clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The second clip, we'll withdraw that at this point this time, Your Honours. The first clip is the one we're primarily interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In the first clip we have an interview of Mr. Seselj with a journalist just before Mr. Seselj goes to The Hague after having heard of the indictment against him. That's what this clip is all about. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to the best of my recollection I commented on the entire text of the indictment, but here they only showed what concerned Hrtkovci. But tell me tell you something, I must correct something that is stated in the indictment, that list of Croats to be expelled was read out. That's a lie. There were Croats who had already gone and joined the Croatian armed forces. I say here that I read it out, but it actually wasn't me. It was an activist from my party. It comes to the same thing, as if I had read it out. If an activist of my party reads something out, it's the same as if I had read it out. But later on I may show this entire video in the courtroom because we do have the video of this rally in Hrtkovci. But I have a comment on all of this by your leave. In 2003, up to the first half of 2004, I received video material from the OTP on videotapes. Then they started sending me DVDs and I refused those. I had the intention of refusing videotapes as well, because instead of transcripts they gave me interviews with various witnesses and suspects. I refused to accept anything that was on DVD. Now that you've made it possible for me to receive all relevant material on paper, transcripts of interviews, statements, and so on, everything that traditionally belongs to typical court documentation, I am now asking the OTP to disclose to me all the video clips that they have at their disposal in their original version so that my associates can search through it and find parts that are interesting for us but that the OTP has kept quiet about. So I'm asking for all the video material which really and truly is video material, not, for example, an interview with General Panic of a thousand pages for me to look at and listen to. No. What I want is video clips, footage that was taken in particular times and places relevant for this indictment, like the material we've seen today. I think this is very important for my defence and that under Rule 68(i) the OTP's duty-bound to disclose that to me. So I'm asking for all the footage they received from the Croatian authorities, the Muslim authorities from Bosnia, all three Serbian authorities that this be disclosed to me in a reasonable time. There are video clips here that I find very valuable for my defence which I didn't know existed, and who knows what else they have at their disposal that I have never seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before addressing this point, we need a number for the last clip, for the last video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P00300. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, I'm trying to understand what Mr. Seselj is requesting. He explained that during the pre-trial stage, and you know that several Judges were in charge of that stage, several Trial Chambers, in any case, at some point he received VHS videos, he viewed them, and then he was sent DVDs, and he refused as a principle to play these DVDs, to view them. Today he's telling us that he's discovering these videos for the first time, and he wants the Prosecution to disclose to him all the video material, all the relevant video material that is at the disposal of the Prosecution. He's requesting the originals. So I suppose he means that these videos should be given to him in his own language. If a video is in English, he should be provided with the transcript or the text in B/C/S for him to be able to follow what's being said in French, German, English, or whatever. He is asking you to disclose the videos that are in possession of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. I don't even insist on having subtitles. I just want original footage not something that they are duty-bound to give me on paper, to have me exert myself and have this put on paper and so on and so forth, but original footage of historical events. It doesn't have to be subtitled. We'll find our way around it. I just want to have that material as soon as possible so we can start searching it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you want to receive them as DVDs?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, my associates can operate DVDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're trying to check some disclosure receipts, Your Honours, but I believe that on two occasions we've tried to provide this material and Dr. Seselj's refused to accept it so I don't know if he's talking about the same video material or different video material. I will say that the Office of the Prosecutor has undertaken a huge effort to digitise all video material for the simple reason that videotape has a very short -- relatively speaking, a very short lifespan. And many of the videotapes, the original videotapes, when you go to play them there's simply nothing left on them because over the course of the past 15 to 18 years, they've simply deteriorated, if you will, the images on the videotape. So if we're talking about actual videotapes, some of them, there's nothing left on the videotapes. So as a result of that, we have virtually digitised all video material. So the only way to get most of that material would be on DVDs in digital format. Now, I'm not sure if Dr. Seselj is talking about what we've tried to disclose to him I believe twice which he's refused to accept because it was digitised video rather than videotapes, or if he's referring to something else. So if we could perhaps get a clarification of exactly what it is he wants, but I believe it needs to be very clear that most if not all of this material has been digitised for the simple reason that the videos are in the -- are in the process of deteriorating because videotape, unfortunately, does not have an indefinite lifespan, and some of this material I know from dealing on other cases has deteriorated to the point where it is simply impossible to watch. So videotape as an option, something you put in a VCR machine, very well might not even be an option with respect to some of this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, apparently when the Prosecution started collecting evidence they were given videotapes by various governments, NGOs, by Ms. Kandic, by X, Y, or Z. As time went by, because this Tribunal has been around for more than 10 years already, some of these tapes deteriorated, because most of us might know that it's a process that happens with time, and because of that the Prosecution decided to digitise all these videotapes and to put them in digital format, on DVDs. They've started that, they might not have completed the exercise. In other words, some DVDs in digital format were sent to you and you refused them. Before making any request today, it might be a good idea for your associates to view all the DVDs you refused to accept. After that, you may be in a position to ask for additional material, because I believe that you yourself never viewed this footage. You never even received this footage because you refused it. Is that -- is that the position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Mundis is relatively new to this case, and he doesn't know all the trouble I had in the first four years. Then the Pre-Trial Judges and Trial Chambers and Prosecutors kept deciding to send me all the material in electronic format. For example, along with expert Davor Strinovic there was a vast quantity of documents. They wanted to send them all to me on DVD. Then they are duty-bound to give me transcripts of testimony from other cases for witnesses called here. They wanted to give me all of that in electronic form. The only way for me to oppose this is to categorically refuse to accept anything in electronic format. You are now guaranteeing that I will receive all these materials on paper and in the Serbian language. This now opens up the possibility for me to accept video material which is original footage of historical events, footage of myself making a speech, visiting the front lines, and so on and so forth. Footage of our volunteers, footage taken in these situations. I accept all of that on DVD. I continue refusing to accept anything that I should get on paper such as, for example, testimony from previous cases and so on and so forth. I don't want the Prosecutor to see a chance here now of foisting off on me DVDs with interviews of suspects or witnesses, witness testimony from other cases, and so on and so forth. I think I've been quite clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I understand. It's rather complex, but I will try to sum up the issue. Initially the Prosecution sent all, and I insist all material, everything, on DVDs. I'm talking about documents, transcripts, video footage, and so on and so forth. This was sent to either him or to his standby counsel. As you know he went on a hunger strike, and then we started everything from scratch. From then on, he received the material coming under Rule 68 in his own language and in -- on paper, material related to Rule 66 or 68, but now we are faced with a problem. Those videos were initially mixed with all the rest, with all the other materials, and now he wants to have this video footage on DVDs. I suppose what the Prosecution should do is to look at all these DVDs that were sent to him to try identify the video footage that is on these DVDs, and the Prosecutor should now -- and that's a positive development, and I believe that as the day's gone by things will develop positively. So now Mr. Seselj has decided to accept DVDs with video footage related to historical facts. For example, when he went to the front, when he dealt with such-and-such person who's mentioned in the indictment. That's the way I understand his request. Is the Prosecution in a position to go through the hundreds or thousands of DVDs that were initially disclosed to the accused, is the Prosecution, in order to do this for the Prosecution to then send him only the video footage on DVDs?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would need to check, but I am being informed by my case manager that there were 15 DVDs that contained exclusively video material, that contained -- these 15 DVDs contained more than 100 hours of what might be described as historical or contemporaneous video material. That we have tried to disclose to the accused on two separate occasions, 27 September 2007 and again on 30 October 2007. This contains all of the material on the 65 ter list. We certainly -- it would take us many, many weeks if not months to go through all of the video material that the OTP possesses looking for specific things that the accused might be interested in. I would respectfully suggest as a starting point that Dr. Seselj accept, if he has not accepted thus far, or review, if he and his associates have not reviewed it thus far, the 100 plus hours of videotape material contained on the 15 DVDs. If he needs another copy, we have a copy of it upstairs and it can be in his hands within a matter of hours at most. Certainly by the end of today. If there is additional material that he wants that is not contained in these 15 DVDs, I will certainly -- or sorry I'm now being told it's 12 DVDs not 15. So I stand corrected. These 12 DVDs, I would certainly entertain a letter from Dr. Seselj asking me for more specific videos if he can tell me I'm looking for this material from this from this time period, that would be helpful. He can write us a letter in Serbian. We'll read the letter. We'll see what we can do and respond to it. But everyone needs to understand we have thousands and thousands and thousands of hours of videotape, many of which are compilation tapes covering the entire conflict in the former Yugoslavia and it's simply not possible to sit down and review each and every one of those tapes in any kind of a timely manner. So I would strongly suggest that we start with the material that we've tried to give him, those 12 DVDs, and if he knows of specific interviews he gave or specific footage that he is aware of, I will check the archives and we will disclose that to him in a digital format on a DVD. I think that's the most practical, reasonable, and expeditious way to go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is once again a positive development. Mr. Seselj, the Prosecution is telling us that there are 12 DVDs which amount to a hundred hours and that this was sent to you. If you have misplaced them, the Prosecution can give you another copy. Now, from a technical and tactical standpoint, it would be advisable for you, perhaps not for you solely because a hundred hours is quite a long time for your associates to view all of this, and that under your authority afterwards you could then say that some videos are missing relating to historical facts, historical events, and important personalities. Mr. Mundis is quite open about this and is prepared to read any letter coming from you, and this cannot be levelled against the Prosecution. There are -- they have hundreds and thousands of documents to review, thousands and ten thousands of viewing time, and we cannot ask Mr. Mundis and Mr. Mussemeyer to 24 hours a day be rooted in front of their screens and tell you what this contains. Now, just by way of an example, in the case of Mr. Kameni, perhaps certain videos in which one can see Mr. Kameni, perhaps some of these videos are useful. So this is a twofold response. First of all, please check out these 12 DVDs that amount to a hundred hours of viewing time, and then when you make your requests, make very concise requests to enable the Prosecution to conduct the appropriate researches.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... acceptable to me, but you were a Pre-Trial Judge when on one occasion I calculated and came up with a figure of 800 hours that I would need to review all the material concerning other cases that at the time the OTP wanted to hand over in the electronic form to me. This was absolutely not feasible. Now we have reduced that to the historical video material. I'm going to accept these 12 DVDs and my associates are going to prepare a request for some other things that we might be interested in. I believe that this video material is not protected, that it is all public. So the OTP will probably not have a problem providing us with a list of everything that they possess so as to enable us to see what we might be interested in. I suppose that they have a list of everything that they have in their possession, so all in all the 12 DVDs plus a list of everything else they have and we will have a successful cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know that. I have some experience in this Tribunal. Unless some of the videos have been tendered under seal in some other cases, then if you were to disclose this then an application should be made before the Chamber. This might complicate matters. This is just a textbook example. Let's, for instance, take the case of an ICRC document and that this video document has been used in a particular case because the ICRC may or may not have had protective measures and that this document is under seal. In that case, the Prosecutor needs to look into the problem. I don't know. This is purely theoretical. You have told us that you are going to view all these DVDs, you together with your associates, and you are going to be making precise applications to the Prosecutor to obtain one or other video, and from then on the Prosecutor can conduct his own searches if he can. If he can't, well then he won't be able to meet your requests.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And a list of all the things that they have in their possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One other thing, Mr. Mundis. Does the OTP have a register in which you have recorded all the videos as they came in, which would be easier for you? For instance, if a video came from Vukovar, this might be registered as Vukovar BBC, CNN, Sky News, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ideally, that's the way it should work. I will state the following, perhaps Your Honours are aware of this from other cases: All of the evidence registration numbers, the ERN numbers, the 16-digit numbers that are assigned to each piece of evidence, any ERN number that begins with V is a video. So I can certainly generate a list of all the videos -- the ERN of all the videos that we possess. If the videotape was provided to the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 70, it should have -- the first digit or the first figure in the ERN number should be R. Any ERN number beginning with R is a Rule 70 document. A video that came under Rule 70 should be stamped with an R rather than a V. That means I should be able to generate a list of all the videos in the possession of the Prosecution. Now, the issue then becomes -- because certainly a list with however many thousands ERN numbers beginning with V is of little or no value to anyone. The issue then becomes what type of description I can pull out of the database that could be provided and which would in any way be helpful to the accused. Virtually all of the investigations undertaken by this office in the initial stages prior to indictment had a code-name. Most of the investigators would have logged the material in under that investigative code-name. So it's not always the case that you can tell by simply looking at the description what geographic area or what crime base or what the document or the video relates to. So it will really depend in part on the quality of the descriptions of the person who entered that material into evidence. I'll have to check on that. I don't know how long it will take for me to extract that information out of the database. I certainly -- it would seem -- it would seem standing here at this moment it would certainly be easier for us to provide such a list to the accused and to have him indicate what material he wants than for him to provide us with a letter which we then go and search. So if the easiest thing, the most reasonable step, the most practical way of getting this material to Dr. Seselj and the most timely way is for us to give him a list and for him and his associates to, in effect, tick box what they want and get that back to us, that that very well might be the easiest way to do it. Again, having said that, I need to go back and determine first of all what that list would look like if we just pull it out of a database because the descriptions might be such that it makes absolutely no sense to anyone outside of OTP. Of course that list is going to be in English and if it's -- if it's a 900-page long list of videos and we have to translate that into Serbian, that's going to take us a long time to do. So it's not something that I can just go back to my office and push a couple of buttons and out is going to come a list of videotapes that is going to make any sense to Dr. Seselj or members of his team. I can't tell you that that's going to be the case standing here now. I will have to go make some inquiries. I will have to determine how long this list is. I will have to determine if in fact I'm going to be ordered or requested to give that to him in Serbian. Then that's going to take a significant period of time for me to produce and generate a list like this in Serbian.
