And it could very well be a question of weeks and months before I could do that depending on how long the list is and how much there is in the description field for each of these videos. So I'm certainly prepared to do what I can to get this material to the accused, but I'm going to need to make some inquiries and come back to the Chamber at some point next week once I have a better handle on what it is that we could produce in terms of a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, if I have understood you correctly, the videos are referenced as -- under number V or R, and Rule 70 videos and then you have a set of figures. You're able to provide such a list and you can disclose that to Mr. Seselj, but to make it more useful, let's assume you have something that begins with the letter V. Would you be able to tell us whether it relates to Zvornik, the JNA, the volunteers, so that he is able to identify it? If you just give V with a series of numbers, that will not be very evocative. Is your database sufficiently efficient? Is there a description of the video together with these numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's what I was trying to explain, Your Honour. It depends in part on the investigator or analyst who in effect obtained this material and what type of description they gave to it. Again, all of the investigations in the pre-trial phase, pre-indictment phase went by code-names so that we could discuss them without other people knowing what they were all about. Some investigators will have logged that in and it will say video material relevant to the Tusk [phoen] investigation, for example. That will have absolutely no meaning to -- to Dr. Seselj or members of his team. That will tell me, as someone in OTP, everything I need to know about what case that tape concerns. So I'm going to need -- I'm going to need to do a little bit of homework here in terms of what those descriptions look like, what type of information I can pull out of the database, what this spreadsheet that is going to be produced is going to look like, how many hundreds or thousands of pages is it going to run to because of the detail or lack thereof of the descriptions, et cetera. So I don't -- the short answer is I don't know until I have the chance to have members of the staff in effect produce a -- produce a dummy chart for me to look at and see if that's something that's going to helpful at all in terms of the descriptive fields and what I can pull out of the database. So I don't know what this list will look like. I don't know how long this list will be. I don't know if those descriptive fields are going to be sufficient to allow Dr. Seselj to make any sense out of it. Once I'm able to do that, perhaps next week I can come back with a sample, if you will, and show everyone what this type of list would look like, give you an indication of how many pages it would be. And as I said, if I'm going to be ordered or required to produce that in the Serbian language, then we're going to be talking about an exercise that obviously is going to take many months before in all likelihood before we're able to produce such a thing. And again, that's going to mean other transcription or translation projects will have to be re-evaluated because we do have, you know, limited translation resources available to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's assume you identify a video which is related to Zvornik and involves volunteers. Well, that's not going to take months. The purpose for Mr. Seselj, as far as I can see, well, for him it's important to have a list and the titles of the videos, and then he can say whether he's interested or not, and if he's interested, then he will ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show you my goodwill and make your job easier, sir. Yesterday I insisted on this being submitted to me in Serbian for principle reasons and I hope that you have all understood why I insisted. I can accept your list in English because all the names are in Serbian, all the geographical name locations -- locations are in Serbian and the times and the dates I understand. The timing is very important here. Even if it is delivered to us in English, if it is delivered to us as soon as possible, that's okay, but do not, please, believe that from now on everything else will be accepted in English. In order to make your life easier, I will now accept for this material to be accepted in English but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... chapter, Mr. Mundis will conduct his research work and get back to you. As soon as he has prepared a list, he will disclose this list to you. Now we have to finish, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, there is another problem that I wish to raise. I also have at my disposal certain video footages that are relevant for the events and the times pertaining to the indictment. I want to show some of the video footages in my cross-examination of these -- of some witnesses. However, there is a procedure in the detention unit that disallows me to do so. According to the procedure in place, every DVD has to be inspected and it is only then that it is decided whether the accused can have it or not. Now I'm asking the registry upon your request to find a solution. When my legal advisors bring DVDs to me that they are able to hand them over directly to me maybe with a sticker like the registry does for the video footages of the trial so that nobody can take these videos from me. I have to personally determine which videos I'm going to use and which not. Why should the prison administration be allowed to view all these before me? I believe that this violates the essential rights arising from my defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Together with the legal officer of the Trial Chamber we would look into the matter and see whether this is feasible or not, because as you know, the prison commander is responsible for anything that comes in and that leaves the prison. In my country, the relationship between an accused and his lawyer, well, this is a privileged relationship and is confidential, but in case I'm not quite sure because the administration of the prison may say if I don't check to see what's in it, I don't know what it may contain. This could perhaps jeopardise order and security. I don't know. I'm not able and I don't think my colleagues on the Bench are able to provide you with an answer today, but we will let you know as soon as possible. We have a few minutes left. We have two witnesses that are going to be coming next week - I won't tell you whether there are any protective measures or not - which means that on Tuesday we shall start at 8.30, and the legal officer will tell you how much time will be granted to the Prosecution and the accused for his cross-examination. That's right. There are two witnesses who are going to be coming next week, Mr. Mundis; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please be given their pseudonyms at least because I don't know who they are. One is a BS and the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're going to learn that straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's -- that's exactly what I wanted to say. On Tuesday carrying over into Wednesday, the Prosecution will call VS-1013. That's 1013. We would expect his evidence to begin on Tuesday and carry over into Wednesday. On Wednesday, then, we would call VS-1015. That's 1015 to commence on Wednesday and hopefully to finish on Thursday, the 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. How much time, Mr. Mundis? How much did you ask for 1013?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe we asked for three hours for 1013, and we had initially asked for two hours for 1015. I believe we might need a little bit more time for 1015, but of course we're entirely in the Chamber's hands in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll see. And the legal officer will tell you by e-mail at the earliest convenience. Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still need to say that there is nothing about VS-33 and this was announced on Thursday. It is only now that I learn that these two witnesses that you have just mentioned will appear next week and I never heard that before, just so that you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, next week we'll have VS-1013 and VS-1015. That's for certain. Very well. We shall reconvene on Tuesday at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of March, 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.
